Hi Friends,

Earlier this week, I published my first piece in _The Wall Street Journal_ , arguing that if America wants to remain competitive in the global AI race, we need to be willing to build the infrastructure that makes AI possible. Communities should have a say in what gets built, but addressing those concerns doesn't have to mean stopping construction altogether. Gov. Josh Shapiro offered a smart model in Pennsylvania last week, announcing new rules that strengthen local oversight and transparency while still allowing the state to compete for the jobs and investment that come with AI infrastructure.
That's the middle ground we need

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

I've been running around the state, and I'm so full of gratitude.
We've spent the summer criss-crossing North Carolina on the Make Stuff Cost Less campaign tour - from Graham to Wilson to Asheville and more stops along the way.
We're pounding the pavement and putting on the mileage because winning this battleground Senate race means reaching every voter we can across the state.
Now that we're less than 70 days out from the election, we can't pump the brakes anytime soon - but all this traveling comes with a hefty price tag. We need to raise $2 million before our end-of-month deadline on Monday night to fuel next month's leg of the tour, so I have to ask: **[Can you please chip in $5 today to help us keep campaigning across the Tar Heel state?](https://substack.com/redirect/08e9978e-271b-46fc-8d4f-13b31d92d94a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/08e9978e-271b-46fc-8d4f-13b31d92d94a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
While talking with North Carolinians face-to-face, I keep hearing versions of the same thing at every stop:
🚨Basic necessities like groceries and gas are unaffordable for many.
🏠Buying a house seems impossible, especially for younger people.
🇺🇲There are those who believe the American Dream feels unattainable.
In short: **Stuff costs too much, and politicians in Washington DC don 't seem to care.**
When I hear that, I know it's time to get to work - because we can do so much better. This campaign is about making sure voters know exactly what I plan to do as their next U.S. Senator.
I'm in this fight to put people before power, party and politics - just as I did over my eight years as Governor, by expanding Medicaid for hundreds of thousands of working North Carolinians, adding good-paying jobs, increasing teacher pay, expanding paid parental leave and more.
Now, I'm ready to keep up the fight in the U.S. Senate - but getting there won't be easy. The GOP is flooding the airwaves with false attacks, so we need to keep showing up across North Carolina and winning folks onto our side. That said, staying on the road like this takes money (gas, materials, organizers), and our budgeting deadline is just hours away.
Every dollar we get toward our Make Stuff Cost Less tour goal will keep us on the road and meeting the voters who will decide this race - so, if you're able, [will you chip in $5 now](https://substack.com/redirect/08e9978e-271b-46fc-8d4f-13b31d92d94a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), or anything you can to help us get there before our end-of-month deadline on Monday?
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/08e9978e-271b-46fc-8d4f-13b31d92d94a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thanks for all you do,
Roy Cooper

That promise has been invoked exactly once in seventy-seven years. **[_FIND OUT WHEN_](http://links.m.dems-give.org/u/click?_t=ec909c9f9a334fa7ab1c27ba57656538&_m=8c9a2433826942608878e66b6272f7a3&_e=TFTKlFLN3GWdX0H4MIRlctobNYnga8Gc4d64sUMV8u0HmQ6-oRvCYMFsnhRIHqBI5Zn-3QORCh0nytld3hKbm6E2cK0o0Ui2RV06aq6Q7VQ5qsUSEJ0M6JaztBfLKkgJKCQtaKzwVsUkq5SZtYBNZTRg6IdC2xjJGoTdm678mwlN89ctXOLNTgToopdVhHPyAiNbDvkVIC8l3KN0M89bmWLHKHYOTp3gxVwBvwRSp7-2NGzHcDYwLpa-3iKhmKH480RtPkHy95B-jYBmQVOyYE6-ZgFQcoVapWEwJb0DgWv1S-32cyXv14WYM2bDX-H18yJzYQOcKOTByalS-G78uvqHqJhOw9kTpw7z90cbuksWruYgXpyPFxEZLFFEthbqp-rz1DPj0VDM3-72tZB0bQNDKOI14gicU42aD2jaXrWdHdOeCgL8nLMBrdN02wYCwN54N98twWr3lC7YzWtiq3DxjFwe0Tyja4511v_PMl4WOHfLMH38tYFo7AAb46RBOQFBX03AH4Dj3PcjFvr4Kv4fSdRsRILOIKMigRUJmmyDXdxKSzbW7dq99u2yuXHhChzFH18YFmyMqUtq6eat1vHOMTqIqI3zMziu9HwUy_0%3D)** It was invoked for us, the day after September 11th. Allied troops went to Afghanistan because America was hit. Now Trump says allies "let down" the United States by not joining his war with Iran. He has called them cowards. subject: There’s a reason this story mattered to Charlie
body:
Please read this important message
[unsubscribe](https://trk.thedcbugle.com/?xul=65a6x69jow166jo1opkmvmi0dilqh17h4hmm7ass88wpcxpghd9ob5a3y54dypvdfn10fr26tk2axx3q8djzcx6tgdbn625bu&__stmp=tkhgxi&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh)
Please read the message below from our sponsor.
* * *
| | | |
---
| | | Friend,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life’s work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That’s one reason JD Vance’s story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life — a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**
---
[](https://trk.thedcbugle.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tkhgxi&__onlt=h)
---
[ **Support Turning Point USA &**
**Claim Your Copy of _Communion_**](https://trk.thedcbugle.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tkhgxi&__onlt=h)
---
Friend, this book isn’t just about JD Vance’s story...

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most — away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They’re told faith is outdated. They’re told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God’s grace, to find his way back.

That’s what _Communion_ is about...

And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now.

That’s why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought — on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith.

**[And with your gift of $75 or more, we’ll send your limited-edition copy of JD Vance’s book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith_ right away.](https://trk.thedcbugle.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tkhgxi&__onlt=h)**
---
[ **Support Turning Point USA &**
**Claim Your Copy of _Communion_**](https://trk.thedcbugle.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tkhgxi&__onlt=h)
---
Your support does far more than just send you a book...

It helps Turning Point USA reach young people in the very places where faith is under attack.

Because of supporters like you, students on more than 5,000 campuses are hearing something they may not hear anywhere else: a serious defense of faith, truth, and a life rooted in God.

For many of them, that’s the first time anyone has challenged the lies they have been fed.

And for many of them, that’s where their minds begin to change — and so do their lives.

Charlie believed the next generation was worth fighting for.

He believed young people were not beyond reach — they needed someone willing to meet them where this battle is being fought and tell them the truth clearly and directly.

That’s why your support matters.

It helps Turning Point USA keep showing up. And it helps carry forward the mission Charlie gave his life to build.

**[Please stand with Turning Point USA today with a gift of $75 or more. And when you do, we’ll send you _Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith_ as our thank-you.](https://trk.thedcbugle.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tkhgxi&__onlt=h) **
---
[ **Support Turning Point USA &**
**Claim Your Copy of _Communion_**](https://trk.thedcbugle.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tkhgxi&__onlt=h)
---
| | | Now’s the time to act. Now’s the time to restore faith in God and faith in America before another generation drifts even farther from both.

And with you, Charlie's mission will reach further — and touch more young lives — than ever before.
---
**For Charlie,** **The Turning Point USA Team**
---
[](https://trk.thedcbugle.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tkhgxi&__onlt=h)
---
[_**Support Turning Point USA**_](https://trk.thedcbugle.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tkhgxi&__onlt=h)
---
**P.S.** Friend, many young people leave home with a foundation of faith, only to have the culture chip away at it, piece by piece.

JD Vance knows what that struggle looks like.

So do countless young Americans who Turning Point USA is reaching right now.

**[With your gift of $75 or more today, you will help us reach more of them with truth — and we will send you a limited-edition copy of _Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith_ as our thank-you.](https://trk.thedcbugle.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tkhgxi&__onlt=h)**

| | | I've faced a lot of hatred in my time in public life. I want to tell you about some of it — not for sympathy, but because I think it says something important about this moment.
When I first ran for Congress, there were people who tried to paint me as un-American simply because of where I was born. There were questions about whether someone with a name like mine could really represent this country.
More recently, a sitting Republican elected official publicly called for the mass deportation of Indians and labeled me a "foreign occupier" with an "unpronounceable name."
In Frisco, Texas, a demonstrator tore an Indian flag to pieces while a crowd around them chanted anti-India hatred.
This comes from anyone who has decided that people like me — immigrants, people with hard-to-pronounce names, people who don't fit some narrow idea of who belongs — don't have a right to be here, let alone lead.
_**Every single time, I've made the same choice: Keep going.**_
Because I know exactly what they're trying to do. They want to make people like me feel small, afraid, and unwelcome enough to quit. To go quiet. To let someone else do the fighting.
I refuse.
That's exactly why I started Equal Opportunity Now — to find and support leaders who have faced this same hatred and refused to be intimidated by it. Leaders who understand that extremism, wherever it comes from, only wins if we let it stop us.

clean_body: | | | | = | | | I've faced a lot of hatred in my time in public life. I want to tell you about some of it — not for sympathy, but because I think it says something important about this moment. When I first ran for Congress, there were people who tried to paint me as un-American simply because of where I was born. There were questions about whether someone with a name like mine could really represent this country. More recently, a sitting Republican elected official publicly called for the mass deportation of Indians and labeled me a "foreign occupier" with an "unpronounceable name." In Frisco, Texas, a demonstrator tore an Indian flag to pieces while a crowd around them chanted anti-India hatred. This comes from anyone who has decided that people like me — immigrants, people with hard-to-pronounce names, people who don't fit some narrow idea of who belongs — don't have a right to be here, let alone lead. Every single time, I've made the same choice: Keep going. Because I know exactly what they're trying to do. They want to make people like me feel small, afraid, and unwelcome enough to quit. To go quiet. To let someone else do the fighting. I refuse. That's exactly why I started Equal Opportunity Now — to find and support leaders who have faced this same hatred and refused to be intimidated by it. They are trying to do this in secret for a reason: **they know that selling off Yosemite is politically radioactive.** At Public Land Warriors, we are building the rapid-response infrastructure to expose these backroom deals and turn this corporate land grab into a massive electoral liability. We are going to ensure that every voter knows exactly who is trying to turn our national heritage into a private driveway. | | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

We have just **67 days** to get our message into every corner of PA-11 and make sure voters know they have a choice on November 3.
| | Reaching voters takes resources. Billboards, digital and traditional media advertising, mail, signs, and organizing across the district all cost money. **Your contribution today** will help us reach more voters and build the campaign we need to win!

| [ DONATE TODAY ](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsEag4ErLzpEhPxLt9QUXR/tsMsC80ON6VD)
---

**Recent Polls Show Momentum for PA Democrats, and Nancy Mannion is No Exception!**
Two statewide surveys conducted in August found Democrats leading with public sentiment.
The [Franklin & Marshall College (F&M)’s poll](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsF30mRHkLv9rg1BGyPEFV/VTIctb9QRuVm) found that 48% of registered Pennsylvania voters planned to support a Democrat in their U.S. House race, compared with 36% for a Republican. A [New York Times/Philadelphia Inquirer/Siena survey](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsFVLUdi8i151w50enNxxZ/CI6SsgBBG8d_) reported a similar Democratic advantage, 51% to 44%.
In PA-11, a Democratic win would be historic. No Democrat, or woman, has ever represented Lancaster County in the U.S. House of Representatives.
Affordability, which Nancy is laser-focused on, is a central theme for registered voters in the F&M results:

* 31% identified the economy as Pennsylvania’s most important problem;
* 44% said they were financially worse off than a year earlier;
* 57% reported difficulty paying utility bills; and
* 55% said they had difficulty paying for groceries.

Among voters who ranked the economy as the leading issue, 47% said Democrats were better equipped to address it, while only 23% chose Republicans.
“This data confirms what I’m hearing on the ground in Lancaster and York counties. People across the political spectrum want a representative who shows up, who listens, and who is accountable to their constituents,” Mannion said. “Congressman Lloyd Smucker isn’t that representative. These polls show that people know it, and they’ve had enough. This includes people who have voted for him – they feel let down and frustrated. They want change.”
Additionally, 83% of those polled by F&M intend to vote in November’s General Election.

---

Help us grow our community by forwarding this email to friends, family, and neighbors. **Was this email forwarded to you?** Sign up to receive Nancy's campaign updates directly in your inbox. | [ Sign Up for Weekly Updates → ](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsFxgCq8X470CC8q2cMhfd/IkKPAtOnRIRe)
---
**PA-11 Polling Reveals Similar Patterns**
An August Public Policy Polling survey commissioned by Nancy Mannion’s campaign found similar patterns in Pennsylvania’s 11th Congressional District:

* 46% of registered voters – including 54% of independents – said it was time for a new representative.
* Only 39% of voters said Republican incumbent Lloyd Smucker should be reelected, down 24 points from his election results in 2024.

Of those surveyed, 51% were Republican, 27% were Democrat, and 22% were Independent voters.
That level of support exceeds the Democratic candidates’ vote share in PA-11 in each of the past three election cycles and it shows that Mannion’s campaign has momentum.
Nancy is confident, emphasizing that victory will be a collective effort. “We can win this—not me, we.”
“We – that is everyone in PA-11 who’s fed up with daily strains on family budgets, wars of choice, and harmful healthcare policies based on wild theories that this administration – and Smucker by his support of it – have inflicted on everyone. “

**Help us turn this momentum into victory – let’s send Nancy to Washington!**
As the campaign enters its final stretch, we need your help reaching undecided voters, young people, and anyone who doubts that their voice or vote matters. These three surveys illustrate a growing demand for change, and Nancy is prepared to represent PA-11’s priorities in Congress!
---
$100 buys 500 door hangers$300 buys 100 yard signs$500 lets us reach up to 15,000 people on Meta$4,400 buys a 4-week billboard
---

**Polling Methodology******
* F&M surveyed 501 registered Pennsylvania voters from Aug. 17–23 by telephone and online; the reported margin of sampling error was plus or minus 5.5 percentage points.
* The Times/Inquirer/Siena survey interviewed 760 registered Pennsylvania voters from Aug. 17–21; the reported margin of error was plus or minus 5.2 percentage points.
* Public Policy Polling conducted the poll for the Mannion campaign from Aug. 18 – 19. The firm reached 533 registered voters in Pennsylvania's 11th Congressional district: 51% Republican, 27% Democrat, and 22% Independent. The reported margin of error was plus or minus 3.9 percentage points.

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.

Now, Coach Tuberville is running for Governor so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in his homestate of Alabama. The Radical Left thinks they can flip Alabama blue and turn it into the California of the South. Can he count on your support? _

Peter, Our campaign ads are on the air right now, and with less than 70 days until Election Day, we need the resources to keep them there. That matters because this race is still a toss-up. News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong.

---
| Letter from the Chair
---
| Fellow Nebraska Republicans,
This fall the Republican National Committee is doing something that has never been done before: a national midterm convention. On September 9 and 10 in Dallas, the party will gather at American Airlines Center for a two-night primetime showcase of President Trump's record, the candidates who will carry it forward, and the choice facing voters on November 3.
RNC Chairman Joe Gruters has called it historic. President Trump will appear both nights and deliver the closing keynote on Thursday. Vice President JD Vance headlines Wednesday. Each hour is built around a clear theme: working-family tax relief, border security, trade and American manufacturing, healthcare affordability, lower prescription drug costs, and policies that put families first--including no tax on tips, overtime, and Social Security. Everyday workers and families who have seen results will share the stage alongside candidates from competitive races.
That is the message Nebraska needs to hear and amplify. Our state convention this summer showed Republicans here are activated and ready. Senator Pete Ricketts, Congressmen Mike Flood and Adrian Smith, Attorney General Mike Hilgers, Treasurer Joey Spellerberg, Auditor Mike Foley, Secretary of State nominee Scott Petersen, CD2 nominee Brinker Harding, and RNC Co-Chair KC Crosbie all made the same point: we win when we talk about results and contrast them with a Democratic Party drifting further left. Dallas will put that contrast on national television.
The convention is also a candidate platform. Nightly showcases from 6 to 7 p.m. will introduce Republicans running in the races that decide control of Congress. For Nebraska that means more national attention on keeping our delegation strong and sending reinforcements to Washington who will back tax relief, secure borders, and common-sense energy and agriculture policy that our farmers and ranchers depend on.
Tickets have been allocated through state parties, and--for the first time--the RNC opened a public lottery so grassroots Republicans can attend. Winners were to be notified September 4 at GOPConvention.com. Whether you are in the hall or watching from home, treat those two nights as a kickoff, not a spectator event.
Between now and November, the work is here in Nebraska. County victory rallies, the Five County BBQ, the annual Pete Ricketts Steak Fry, and local campaign walk programs matter more than any speech in Dallas. Watch the convention. Share the stories of tax cuts, border security, and lower drug costs. Volunteer. Talk to neighbors who sat out last time. Then vote--and take someone with you.
President Trump's team and the RNC are putting the American comeback on display. Nebraska Republicans know how to finish the job.
Onward to November. Together We Win!
In Liberty and in Truth,
Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

clean_body: I hope you’ll read this personal letter I wrote you. I hope you’ll read this personal letter I wrote you. | Patriot, In May, I was taken to the hospital, fell into a coma, placed on a ventilator, and read my last rites. And yet, here I still am. In so many ways, it’s miraculous. But ever since my brush with death, I’ve been thinking a lot about my life’s work, my legacy... I fought the Mafia, I fought violent criminals, I fought corruption, and I fought the Deep State agents who tried to frame and destroy my client and friend – President Trump. But today, as an 82-year-old man, I see that my greatest fight still lies ahead. Perhaps I was saved for a very specific reason – to ensure the Radical Left can never again do to anyone else what they’ve done to President Trump and me. And now, I have the chance to WIN that battle. You see, a vengeful Democrat Attorney General is making me stand in yet another RIGGED trial for bogus state-level crimes, because she knows that not even President Trump can save me with a federal pardon in state court. And my “crime?” Refusing to denounce the TRUTH. This trial really is the Left’s last-ditch effort to try and get me to finally throw in the towel. But they simply don’t understand. They can strip me of all I’m worth – all I’ll ever be worth – but what I REFUSE to surrender to the Democrats and their Deep State thugs is my LEGACY! I’d rather lose everything than betray what I know to be true. I could never lie and say what I'm going through is a fair and honest process just to hang on to “earthly possessions.” "For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?" (Mark 8:36) This FINAL BATTLE for my freedom is about ensuring this injustice will NEVER AGAIN happen to another innocent patriot all for standing by what he knows to be right and true. I pray that in the end when we’ve won this trial, that will be my legacy. But now, as I fight with all I’ve got, I have only one place left to turn to help me reach the finish line and secure my freedom: honest and compassionate patriots like YOU. Patriot, I understand this was probably the last thing on your mind today. I get it. And that’s why I always say that if you can’t afford to help me in this fight, please delete this message and carry on with your day. Don’t even think twice about it! But if you can help, I’m going to need the best defense humanly possible to defeat this radical Democrat Attorney General who is hell-bent on locking me up for the rest of my life. Thank you and God bless you, Rudy Giuliani Rudy Defense Trust Paid for by Rudy Defense Trust

## **The Politics of the Meta Settlement**
This week, Meta Platforms agreed to a landmark $18 billion settlement with a bipartisan coalition of state attorneys general.
The historic agreement resolves allegations that the company intentionally designed Facebook and Instagram to addict children and harm their mental health.
[| | | | | Fox News
---
@FoxNews
BREAKING: Meta has reached a $16.68 billion settlement over a landmark lawsuit alleging its social media platforms harmed children. The breaking settlement ends claims against the company as the trial was set to move forward. @JonathanTurley says Meta has the financial
| 1:34 PM * Aug 26, 2026 * 433K Views196 Replies * 276 Reposts * 1.11K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/bd7a9ae8-0cce-4cab-9c95-4d313a94acbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Most of the media attention was rightly focused on the massive financial penalty and the terms of the settlement.
Under the agreement approved by U.S. District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers, Meta must enforce strict new parameters for users under the age of 18:
* **Screen Time Caps:** Teenagers will face a strict two-hour daily limit across Instagram and Facebook combined (which drops to 60 minutes if TikTok and Youtube follow suit).
* **Nighttime Curfews:** Platform access will be completely blocked from midnight to 6 a.m., with app notifications paused overnight between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m.
* **School Hour Silence:** Push notifications will be silenced between 8 a.m. and 3 p.m. on school days to cut down on classroom distractions.
* **Algorithmic Alternatives:** Teens and parents can toggle off recommendation feeds in favor of a chronological feed, disable endless scroll, and remove auto-playing video settings.
* **Strict Oversight:** Meta must remove "like" counts and cosmetic surgery filters for minors, while hiring an independent auditor to monitor compliance and age verification.

Thos policy changes are all great. They represent a massive shift in how tech giants operate.
But policy changes are only part of the story.
The real takeaway is what this means for the 2026 campaign trail.
While the press is focused on the court documents, I want to note the **political impacts** this settlement should have.
Candidates looking to find a hook with voters should be all over this.
Let's get into it. ...

clean_body: Defund the police. Abolish ICE. They're campaigning on it. | Friend, The choice this November could not be more clear. Republicans cut your taxes. We secured the border. We invested in our military. That's what we've delivered. Here's what the Radical Left is offering: defund the police, abolish ICE, protect illegal aliens, and hand your healthcare over to the government. | I used to think "defund the police" was a talking point that got away from them. It's not. I remember when AOC said it herself, on camera: "When we say defund the police, we mean defund the police." That's the DSA platform now, and the DSA platform is running the Democrat Party. They're not walking any of this back. They're campaigning on it. So here’s my warning: If you thought “Woke 1” was crazy, “Woke 2” is going to be much worse if the Democrats win this November. They're telling you exactly what it looks like. Believe them. They've told you what they want. Now I'm telling you what I need: The choice is clear. So is what's at stake. * * *
Hey folks,
My dad, Bill Nellis, is back, which means it's time for another Nellis vs. Nellis--and somehow we agreed on way more than I expected.
We got into Trump's tariff wars, the exploding cost of beef, Flock cameras and government surveillance, ICE, AI data centers, and what happens to working people if AI really does wipe out millions of jobs.
And yes, we still found plenty to fight about.
* [**00:01:43**] We start with Trump trying to rename Lake Ontario--and my Trump-voting dad immediately admits the whole thing is ridiculous before we get into the much bigger problem underneath it: Trump's trade war with Canada.
* [**00:10:03**] My dad lives in Nebraska, where ranchers are feeling the consequences of Trump's policies firsthand. His verdict is pretty simple: Trump says he loves farmers, but "he's not loving the farmers" with what's happening to beef.
* [**00:18:49**] Things get heated over Flock cameras. My dad sees an incredibly useful law-enforcement tool. I see another massive surveillance system that can be abused--and we wrestle with where public safety ends and our right to privacy begins.
* [**00:31:44**] We turn to AI data centers, and this is where the politics are getting really interesting. We talk electricity bills, water, farmland, corporate promises to struggling communities, and why both Republicans and Democrats are starting to question whether these projects are worth the cost.
* [**00:39:01**] Then we hit the question underneath the entire AI debate: what happens if there simply aren't enough jobs anymore? We get into government ownership, universal basic income, job guarantees, and whether America is prepared for the economic disruption coming our way.

This is exactly why I wanted to do Nellis vs. Nellis. My dad and I disagree--a lot--but we actually listen to each other, find places where the politics get more complicated than the talking points, and occasionally discover that we're not as far apart as we thought. If you're exhausted by political conversations designed only to make us hate each other, this one is for you.

--Mike

| | Peter,
---
Flock cameras. By now you've probably heard of them, but even if you haven't, they know all about you. This week I learned that Flock was capturing your private information and storing it. They call it "public safety," but we need to call it what it is — mass surveillance. Flock cameras scan 20 BILLION license plates per month. It's an unprecedented invasion of privacy, and I have some questions. Like, why is this data being collected in the first place? What is it being used for? Who has access to it? And where is it being stored? Protecting your privacy is my priority. I'm getting to the bottom of it, because protecting your privacy shouldn't be controversial or partisan. I'm not fighting for you because it polls well. In fact, there are billion-dollar industries gearing up for a fight to keep spying on you, tracking you, and profiting off your private information. **[I'm fighting against them and for you because it's right — and fights like this don't fund themselves. | | | Five years after January 6, CNN found that Republican nominees for governor in Arizona, Georgia, Michigan, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin have denied, challenged, or cast doubt on Donald Trump’s 2020 loss. If they win, **_each could help shape the 2028 election_**. We have seen this playbook before: cast doubt on a lawful result, undermine public confidence, and then seek more political control over how Americans vote. Governors and secretaries of state make decisions that determine whether voters can trust the system, whether election workers are protected, and whether lawful results are respected. Election denial is not just dangerous rhetoric. [**Will you chip in $10 today to help my campaign defend secure elections and make sure facts—not conspiracy theories—guide this work?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138102055/642988891/-569431239?refcode=260828-5warnings&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmNjEwNzI5NS1mZGEyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=iK-CHS_i2cPNv002U8zU-0-hqMzZH7n_fWlQPwLA3BM=) As Oregon’s Secretary of State, I have stood up to federal overreach, protected sensitive voter information, and defended our secure vote-by-mail system. I will keep doing that, no matter how many threats come from Washington. But what is happening in these five swing states should warn all of us. Extremists are not backing away from election lies. They are trying to gain the offices that could give those lies real power in 2028. This is the responsibility in front of us: protect voters, support election officials, and insist that the rule of law applies even when a candidate does not like the result. [**Please give $25—or whatever you can—today to help me keep public trust stronger than election denial.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138102056/642988892/-569431239?refcode=260828-5warnings&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmNjEwNzI5NS1mZGEyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=iK-CHS_i2cPNv002U8zU-0-hqMzZH7n_fWlQPwLA3BM=) Thank you for standing with me. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. **Friday, August 28, 2026 -**_** ** Israeli strikes kill eight Palestinians in Gaza on Thursday and Friday. Civil defense teams recover 233 bodies in Gaza. Israel bombs house in Jenin in first strike on occupied West Bank in 10 months. Israeli forces raid Nablus; settlers obstruct Friday prayers. Israel detains about 370 Palestinian children, report says. Israeli commander says he is "not sorry" for ordering strike that killed seven World Central Kitchen aid workers. Iran war has depleted Patriot interceptors to "beyond critical" levels. U.S. President Donald Trump expected to meet with American oil refiners. Saudi-backed Yemeni government says soldier killed in Taiz. Israeli violations continue across southern Lebanon. Israel claims Hezbollah launched two explosive drones at troops. Fired Stars and Stripes journalists sue Pentagon over dismissals. Gas industry group boasts of shaping NY Gov. Kathy Hochul's pipeline reversal. U.S. negotiating for stake in Venezuela oil fields. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission finds reasonable cause that Cisco subjected pro-Palestine workers to hostile workplace. UN envoy registers concern with "open-ended Israeli military presence in Syria." Syria's president appoints former Kurdish SDF commander as advisor. Kuwait, Pakistan sign joint defense agreement. Nepal-Tibet flood death toll rises to 552. Sudan's RSF-SPLM-N forces claim capture of two army bases in Blue Nile fighting. Two more U.S. deportees arrive in Eswatini under third-country agreement. Jakarta police detain over 300 after protests. Qatar pledges support for Libyan unity during Benghazi visit. Palestine Action activists charged with "terrorism" offenses over Trump golf course protest._

* * *
# Palestine
* **Israeli strikes kill eight Palestinians in Gaza on Thursday and Friday:** At least four Palestinians were killed in Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip on Friday, according to WAFA. In southern Gaza, three Palestinians from the Abdeen family were killed when an Israeli drone targeted Al-Qarara, northeast of Khan Younis. In Gaza City, an Israeli drone [strike](https://substack.com/redirect/7b760d5f-4b1d-4260-855d-9a3f93103d4c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on a group of Palestinians in the Al-Sabra neighborhood killed one and wounded several others.
* Israel [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/b5c6dd62-208b-48cc-9309-d2c40482321f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) four Palestinians and wounded several others, including children, in attacks across Gaza on Thursday. An Israeli strike on a tent sheltering displaced Palestinians near Gaza City killed one and wounded others. Another Israeli airstrike hit a bicycle in central Gaza City, killing one Palestinian and injuring several.
* Israeli forces shot and wounded a child in Qatar Camp, east of Hamad City.
* **Civil defense teams recover 233 bodies in Gaza:** Gaza's Civil Defense [said](https://substack.com/redirect/e230f78f-60ad-402a-8c6b-4eb139d7c718?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its crews recovered 233 bodies and human remains from beneath the rubble of 20 homes destroyed by Israeli forces in the Gaza governorate, out of 407 people believed to have been buried there. Among those recovered were 73 children and 106 women.
* **Israel bombs house in Jenin in first strike on West Bank in 10 months:** An Israeli military drone struck a house under construction in the Horsh Al-Saada on the western outskirts of Jenin in the occupied West Bank on Friday, as large numbers of Israeli forces entered the area. It marked the first Israeli airstrike on the West Bank in around 10 months. Reporting from the area, Drop Site contributor Mujahed al-Saadi said that the house was struck with at least two missiles and that Israeli troops deployed to the area immediately after the attack, preventing ambulances from reaching the targeted house, and detained Palestinian medical workers who arrived on the scene.
* Three Palestinians were killed in the strike, according to Reuters.
* The Israeli military claimed it had carried out a "precise strike" targeting what it described as "several terrorists." Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu [praised](https://substack.com/redirect/c40f9be5-d03a-4777-bf19-1ea423d5cd79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the strike on X: "I commend our forces for the successful elimination of the terrorists in Jenin. Shabbat shalom!"
* **Israeli forces raid Nablus; settlers obstruct Friday prayers:** Israeli settlers dressed in military uniforms [prevented](https://substack.com/redirect/4d6cb515-3e3d-43fa-8f37-d678b814df8c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Palestinians from attending Friday prayers at the Al-Wali and Al-Haj Hussein mosques in Beit Furik, east of Nablus, WAFA reported. Separately, Israeli forces [raided](https://substack.com/redirect/e2236a18-7c88-4f68-a022-56a0b44395cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the village of Tal, southwest of Nablus, searching homes and detaining one Palestinian and seizing his vehicle.
* On Thursday, Israeli forces fired sound bombs, tear gassed Palestinians, and sparked fires near homes during a raid on the village of Al-Lubban Asharqiya.
* **Israel detains about 370 Palestinian children, report says:** Approximately 370 Palestinian children are imprisoned in Israeli detention centers as of early August, most at Megiddo and Ofer, according to a [report](https://substack.com/redirect/ed96608c-961c-41fa-9aaf-b3294b8ac0ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) published on Thursday by the Palestinian Center for Prisoners Advocacy.
* In the report, children describe Israeli forces raiding their homes at night, taking them away blindfolded and handcuffed, beating and threatening them, and denying them food, water, and bathroom access.
* During interrogation, children reported experiencing prolonged questioning, isolation, sleep deprivation, and threats against their families.
* Inside Israeli prisons, they face overcrowding, insufficient food and hygiene supplies, restricted family visits, and delayed or denied medical treatment.

* **Israeli commander says he is "not sorry" for ordering strike that killed seven World Central Kitchen aid workers: **Nochi Mendel, who ordered three Israeli drone strikes on the World Central Kitchen (WCK) convoy in Gaza in April 2024, defended his decision to Australia's ABC on Thursday, after he was removed from his post over serious failures and breaches of procedure.
* Mendel claimed WCK had "ties to Hamas" and was "not really... innocent," although he acknowledged he did not know of those alleged links when he ordered the attack.
* Israel declined to pursue a criminal investigation against the commander.
* **" Severe food insecurity" in Gaza, according to latest UN figures:** In Gaza, 50% of families say they completely ran out of food at least once in the past month and about one in five families say they are eating only one meal a day, according to the latest [survey](https://substack.com/redirect/29fb0c37-a906-4e20-aac7-d2768aa2fc85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from the World Food Program (WFP). "Indicators of severe food insecurity remain deeply concerning across the Gaza Strip," the WFP said.
* Three-quarters of surveyed households reported difficulties accessing food markets. Among them, 96% cited financial constraints related to cash liquidity shortages. Of those able to access money, 40% reported being unable to afford basic food items due to high prices.
* Nearly half (46%) of surveyed households reported going to bed hungry at least once during the 30 days preceding the survey, with 7% experiencing this more than ten times. Similarly, 50% of households reported completely running out of food at least once during the same period, including 18% who faced this situation more than ten times. Nearly 3% of households reported going an entire day without eating at least once in the past 30 days.
* The daily average number of trucks crossing into Gaza since last year's ceasefire is 217--far below the 600 trucks per day in the ceasefire agreement that went into effect on October 10, 2025.

# Iran
* **Iran 's Araghchi: "Putting diplomacy back on track isn't impossible": **Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Friday he held "creative discussions" with Qatar's prime minister and foreign minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, saying putting diplomacy back on track "isn't impossible."
* In a [post](https://substack.com/redirect/942f989c-f6d0-4073-a5da-ed2041e745d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X, Araghchi said progress hinges on the U.S. understanding that "pressure doesn't work," adding that Washington should "build trust, speak respectfully, acknowledge our rights, and uphold commitments."
* White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt told Fox News on Thursday that, regarding Iran, Trump "continues to retain all options on the table."
* "We've had Operation Epic Fury to destroy their military. Now we have Operation Economic Outcast to destroy their economy," Leavitt said, maintaining that there would be no negotiations until Trump feels that the Iranians might "come to the table in a meaningful way."
* **CENTCOM gives updates on blockade, Hormuz:** U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/9082d94e-a404-48db-95f3-da5e5e40ffdb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday that U.S. forces had "redirected 75 commercial vessels, disabled 3, and boarded 2 to ensure compliance" in the Strait of Hormuz.
* CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper also claimed that U.S. forces had cleared Iranian sea mines from the Strait's internationally recognized shipping lanes, calling it a "major milestone."
* Cooper added that U.S. forces have overseen the safe passage of nearly 1,500 commercial vessels carrying roughly 750 million barrels of crude through the Strait.

* **Rezaei demands U.S. "fulfill Iran's conditions" to reopen Hormuz, threatens U.S. economic interests if blockade continues:** Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei [said](https://substack.com/redirect/7ac7e81d-30fc-4a29-a9f3-f791717fb9c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday that the "U.S. must first take practical steps to fulfill Iran's conditions and then Iran will proceed to open the Strait of Hormuz," according to Iran's Islamic Republic News Agency (IRNA).
* In a separate interview on Lebanon's Manar TV, Rezaei said Tehran is preparing a list of conditions for reopening Hormuz at the request of mediators. Rezaei said the conditions would include ending the war in the region.
* Iran has agreed to a transit corridor with Oman, he added, whereby ships would transit through a designated central channel in the strait if the U.S. meets Tehran's conditions.
* Iran had "fully and transparently" conveyed its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz to Pakistan, which is carrying Tehran's message to Washington, a source told Tasnim on Thursday.
* Separately, Rezaei [said](https://substack.com/redirect/9ae1bc4e-09cf-4c4e-af70-a78564e3b1d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday that Iran would "target U.S. economic interests fully with intensity and force" if the blockade continues, according to state broadcaster IRIB.
* Rezaei also said that Iran is "closely monitoring the developments related to Beirut and its southern suburbs," adding that those areas are Iran's "red lines."

* **Iran war has depleted Patriot interceptors to "beyond critical" levels: **Trump's war with Iran has [depleted](https://substack.com/redirect/fb3ac6e3-c02a-4151-ad4e-e83cc263a499?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Patriot interceptor stocks in Europe to "beyond critical" levels, a U.S. defense official and a NATO official told the Associated Press, as European forces use the same air-defense system to protect Gulf oil infrastructure.
* The Iran war has consumed roughly 1,500 of America's 2,330 Patriot interceptors, or 65% of the stockpile, according to a CSIS estimate. U.S. missiles assigned to Europe have been diverted to the Middle East.
* A U.S. official said Europe lacks enough Patriots to stop a sustained ballistic-missile attack and has "very limited" capacity against even one strike, warning NATO could be forced to "take punch after punch in the mouth."

* **Trump expected to meet with U.S. oil refiners:** Trump is [expected](https://substack.com/redirect/2eeb45ef-d7dc-407b-b23c-6c834442c73b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to meet major U.S. refiners and fuel retailers next week as his administration faces mounting pressure over gasoline prices ahead of November's midterms, Reuters reported. Valero, Marathon Petroleum and PBF Energy are among those expected to attend.
* Trump has previously attacked oil companies benefiting from the price surge. After Exxon and Chevron reported strong second-quarter earnings, he said: "Chevron, too much money. ExxonMobil, too much. Too much money," and called on them to "give some of that back to the public."

# Yemen
* **Saudi-backed Yemeni government says soldier killed in Taiz:** Yemen's internationally recognized government said on Thursday that a soldier in one of its factions had been killed on the Al-Ahtoub front lines in the western countryside of Taiz governorate, as clashes with Ansarallah continue.

# Lebanon
* **Israeli violations continue across southern Lebanon:** Israeli forces [advanced](https://substack.com/redirect/102df1d6-3823-4a55-be77-ecb3124062b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Friday toward Aita Al-Jabal in the Bint Jbeil district in southern Lebanon from the occupied town of Hadatha, setting fires on the outskirts, Lebanon's National News Agency reported.
* On Thursday, Israel [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/954176ab-c2b7-47d1-bb89-2099c834727e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) three airstrikes on Qantara in the Marjayoun district, while Israeli drones dropped several canisters containing explosives on homes in Mansouri in the Tyre (Sour) district.
* Israeli forces also [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/6903ef21-2bf2-4934-93f0-809668636fb0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) white phosphorus near Kfar Roumanne, overnight into Thursday, according to L'Orient.

* **Israel claims Hezbollah launched two explosive drones at troops:** The Israeli military [said](https://substack.com/redirect/42012c3b-b022-400f-bf59-6837dab59305?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Hezbollah launched two "booby-trapped drones" toward Israeli troops operating around the Ali Al-Taher hills overnight Wednesday into Thursday. No casualties were reported.

# U.S. News
* **Trump signs order renaming Lake Ontario "Lake America" amid Canada trade dispute:** President **Donald Trump** [signed](https://substack.com/redirect/9f8d30eb-dcac-46a0-9996-89fa8b7c6122?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an executive order Thursday directing the renaming of Lake Ontario, which borders New York and Canada, to "Lake America," escalating his trade dispute with Canada, according to NPR.
* "We have a gulf, and we have a lake, now all we need is an ocean," Trump told reporters at the Oval Office signing, a reference to his earlier renaming of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America, before blaming Canada directly, calling it "the worst to trade" among U.S. partners.
* The move follows the collapse of trade talks and Trump's imposition of a 50% tariff on some Canadian goods, which prompted Canadian counter-tariffs.
* **Judge again blocks Trump 's mail-in voting order days before ballots ship: **U.S. District Judge **Indira Talwani** [blocked](https://substack.com/redirect/9c11b549-2511-4def-bb4b-4e77c943bdd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) implementation of President Donald Trump's executive order limiting mail voting for two weeks Thursday, halting the directive for a second time about a week before the first midterm mail ballots are due to be sent, according to the Associated Press.
* The ruling came after Democrats and voting rights groups refiled their lawsuits following a Supreme Court decision that let the administration proceed on procedural grounds without ruling on the order's legality.
* Talwani wrote that plaintiff states "have neither time nor funds" to redesign ballots and update election systems to comply with new Postal Service requirements before the midterms.
* **Fired Stars and Stripes journalists sue Pentagon over dismissals:** Three journalists at the federally funded Stars and Stripes news organization [sued](https://substack.com/redirect/0f1fa9e7-bd1f-4cea-a261-676d97f5132d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Pentagon on Thursday, alleging their firings came in retaliation for reporting on worsening conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln during its extended nine-month deployment.
* The lawsuit says the Defense Department moved to fire the reporters a day after Stars and Stripes published an article detailing sailors' food and water shortages, disrupted mail, and poor mental health during the extended deployment.
* One reporter said his termination notice cited a CBS interview in which he called censorship of news for service members "a red line."
* **Gas industry group boasts of shaping NY Gov. Hochul 's pipeline reversal: **Natural Allies for a Clean Energy Future, a public relations group backed by pipeline companies including Williams Companies, told a fossil fuel industry conference in April that it had had "high-level engagement" with Governor **Kathy Hochul** 's office shortly before she reversed her opposition to new gas pipelines in November 2025, according to industry materials [reviewed by The Lever](https://substack.com/redirect/056f584c-0ef7-4a7f-b7d8-4fa7eb028f14?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* **U.S. negotiating for stake in Venezuela oil fields:** The Trump administration is [negotiating](https://substack.com/redirect/4a7a450b-e5d1-40dd-b8d6-0fa375c28efb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with Venezuela's interim government for a stake in more than a dozen oil fields holding an estimated 90 billion barrels, Axios reported on Thursday, citing two U.S. officials.
* Officials say the deal could more than double U.S. proven oil reserves. In return, private companies, including American firms, would redevelop Venezuela's aging infrastructure and direct more oil revenue to Caracas.
* Trump was reportedly considering U.S. ownership of Venezuelan fields before authorizing the January 3 capture of President **Nicol as Maduro**.
* Secretary of State **Marco Rubio** and acting Venezuelan President **Delcy Rodr iguez** are leading the talks, with **Stephen Miller** also involved.
* **EEOC finds reasonable cause Cisco subjected pro-Palestine workers to hostile workplace:** The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission [found](https://substack.com/redirect/d0ca6d36-ed3a-4dec-87dd-094b9f31380e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reasonable cause to believe Cisco violated Title VII by subjecting a class of workers to a hostile environment based on Middle Eastern origin, Muslim faith or association with Muslim and Middle Eastern people.
* An open letter signed by 1,700+ employees urged Cisco to stop supplying technology to Israel's government. The complaint says harassment on Cisco's Inclusive Communities platforms began October 7, 2023, and continued after repeated complaints.
* It also alleges Cisco fired an employee over pro-Palestine efforts, though the EEOC did not make a separate finding on that claim. **[Drop Site reported on the firing last year](https://substack.com/redirect/a63c6737-1338-4d41-89fa-331d2016b2e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**

📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com
# Other International News
* **UN envoy registers concern with "open-ended Israeli military presence in Syria": **Claudio Cordone, the UN deputy special envoy for Syria, told the UN Security Council that he is "concerned by statements from senior Israeli officials advocating an open-ended Israeli military presence on Syrian territory."
* He noted that the Israeli presence violates Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity and is inconsistent with the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, adding that Israeli forces have continued military activity in southern Syria, particularly in Quneitra and Yarmouk Basin.
* **Syria 's president appoints former Kurdish SDF commander as advisor: **Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa has [appointed](https://substack.com/redirect/acdcc32e-2927-4b00-b4ac-0c7372a79d9d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Mazloum Abdi, leader of the now-dissolved Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces, as an advisor to the presidency, state news agency SANA reported.
* The move comes three days after Abdi announced the SDF's dissolution, following its integration into the Syrian military under a deal struck with Damascus in January.
* The U.S.-backed SDF had spearheaded the fight against ISIS and was the largest force still outside the Syrian army.
* **Kuwait, Pakistan sign joint defense agreement:** Kuwait and Pakistan formalized a joint defense agreement during the visit of the Kuwaiti defense minister to Pakistan on Thursday.
* The agreement intends to "strengthen operational coordination, exchange military experiences, and enhance the level of readiness and integration" among the armed forces of both countries, according to representatives from the countries.
* Pakistan's armed forces will assist Kuwait in training and capacity building, according to state-run Pakistan TV, and assist Kuwait with "border management" and "other mutually agreed areas of defense cooperation."
* Pakistan signed a joint defense agreement with Saudi Arabia and Turkey earlier this month.

* **Nepal-Tibet flood death toll rises to 552:** On Friday, Nepal's police announced a new death toll of at least 547 people from Wednesday's floods, while Chinese state media confirmed at least five deaths on the Tibet side, bringing the overall total to 552. 1,924 people remain missing across both sides of the border, including hundreds of foreign nationals, according to a report from Nepal's disaster authority on Friday morning.
* **RSF-SPLM-N forces claim capture of two army bases in Blue Nile fighting:** Sudan's Rapid Support Forces [said](https://substack.com/redirect/03ad7726-b576-4fc9-900c-6c1a33d29330?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Friday its joint force with the Sudan People's Liberation Movement-North captured the Bakori and Surkum army bases in the southeastern Blue Nile region bordering Ethiopia, taking weapons, equipment, and prisoners, according to Sudan Tribune.
* Separately in South Kordofan state, army forces repelled a dawn RSF assault Friday on the town of Tibsa near Abbasiya Tagali, forcing paramilitary fighters to retreat toward Moreib after several hours of clashes.
* **Two more U.S. deportees arrive in Eswatini under third-country agreement:** Two migrants from Latin America deported from the United States [arrived](https://substack.com/redirect/c3fb9c47-7edd-4014-9ebb-c099c4b7748d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Eswatini on Thursday, the fifth such group sent to the southern African kingdom since July 2025.
* The Eswatini government did not identify the deportees, disclose their nationalities, or say how long they would remain.
* The Trump administration has struck third-country deportation agreements with roughly two dozen countries, including about 11 in Africa.
* Eswatini's King Mswati III has long faced accusations of violently suppressing pro-democracy movements in the country.
* **Jakarta police detain over 300 after protests:** Indonesian police [detained](https://substack.com/redirect/dbb91dca-71ba-4532-84c3-13ffa6ecb9d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) more than 300 people, including 160 minors, and named 45 suspects following late-night rioting that erupted after Thursday's anti-government demonstrations near parliament, Reuters reported.
* Jakarta police accused a group of rioters of setting fire to a police post and two motorcycles and of throwing rocks and sticks at officers.
* The police used a water cannon and tear gas against the protesters. A man was found unconscious at the scene and later died at a hospital.
* President Prabowo Subianto's approval rating fell to 38% in a recent Tempo poll over his economic policies.
* **Qatar pledges support for Libyan unity during Benghazi visit** : Qatar's Minister of State Mohammed bin Abdulaziz al-Khulaifi [met](https://substack.com/redirect/faa2c564-2e3c-4dd5-9fcf-fd67a5bb3e8e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with Khalifa Haftar, commander of the eastern-aligned Libyan National Army, in Benghazi, expressing Qatar's support for Libyan sovereignty and "a political process that reflects Libyans' aspirations," according to a Qatari Foreign Ministry.
* Libya, split since 2014 between the Tripoli-based Government of National Unity and the Haftar-backed eastern administration, reached a new pact last week rewriting election laws and setting a 24-month deadline for elections.
* **Palestine Action activists charged with "terrorism" offenses over Trump golf course protest**: Seven Palestine Action activists who spray-painted messages and damaged Trump's Turnberry golf resort in Scotland during a March 2025 protest have been [charged](https://substack.com/redirect/3d76c3cd-f601-45df-8995-7f4bc0257b07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with malicious damage "having a terrorist connection," according to reporting by The Guardian and The New York Times.
* The activists sprayed red paint on the clubhouse, damaged turf and sprinklers, applied weedkiller to greens, and painted "Gaza is not 4 sale" on the property in protest of Trump's stance on Gaza.
* The case comes days after the U.S. Treasury Department imposed sanctions on Palestine Action and the pro-Palestine group Masar Badil, along with financial penalties on the Italian digital services group Autistici Inventati.

Drop Site Daily: August 28, 2026 | | | Aug 28 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Israeli soldiers gather outside a home under construction following a drone strike killing of three Palestinians, on the western outskirts of the northern city of Jenin, in the occupied West Bank on August 28, 2026. Photo by Jaafar Ashtiyeh / AFP via Getty Images. Friday, August 28, 2026 - Israeli strikes kill eight Palestinians in Gaza on Thursday and Friday. Civil defense teams recover 233 bodies in Gaza. Israel bombs house in Jenin in first strike on occupied West Bank in 10 months. Israeli forces raid Nablus; settlers obstruct Friday prayers. Israel detains about 370 Palestinian children, report says. Israeli commander says he is "not sorry" for ordering strike that killed seven World Central Kitchen aid workers. "Severe food insecurity" in Gaza, according to latest UN figures. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi: "Putting diplomacy back on track isn't impossible." U.S. Central Command gives updates on blockade, Strait of Hormuz. Iranian Security Chief Mohsen Rezaei demands U.S. "fulfill Iran's conditions" to reopen Hormuz, threatens U.S. economic interests if blockade continues. Iran war has depleted Patriot interceptors to "beyond critical" levels. U.S. President Donald Trump expected to meet with American oil refiners. Saudi-backed Yemeni government says soldier killed in Taiz. Israeli violations continue across southern Lebanon. Israel claims Hezbollah launched two explosive drones at troops. Trump signs order renaming Lake Ontario "Lake America" amid Canada trade dispute. Judge again blocks Trump's mail-in voting order days before ballots ship. Fired Stars and Stripes journalists sue Pentagon over dismissals. Gas industry group boasts of shaping NY Gov. Kathy Hochul's pipeline reversal. U.S. negotiating for stake in Venezuela oil fields. Nepal-Tibet flood death toll rises to 552. Sudan's RSF-SPLM-N forces claim capture of two army bases in Blue Nile fighting. Two more U.S. deportees arrive in Eswatini under third-country agreement.
