Palestine Action activists charged with "terrorism" offenses over Trump golf course protest. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Palestine Israeli strikes kill eight Palestinians in Gaza on Thursday and Friday: At least four Palestinians were killed in Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip on Friday, according to WAFA. In southern Gaza, three Palestinians from the Abdeen family were killed when an Israeli drone targeted Al-Qarara, northeast of Khan Younis. In Gaza City, an Israeli drone on a group of Palestinians in the Al-Sabra neighborhood killed one and wounded several others. Israel four Palestinians and wounded several others, including children, in attacks across Gaza on Thursday. An Israeli strike on a tent sheltering displaced Palestinians near Gaza City killed one and wounded others. Another Israeli airstrike hit a bicycle in central Gaza City, killing one Palestinian and injuring several. Israeli forces shot and wounded a child in Qatar Camp, east of Hamad City. Civil defense teams recover 233 bodies in Gaza: Gaza's Civil Defense its crews recovered 233 bodies and human remains from beneath the rubble of 20 homes destroyed by Israeli forces in the Gaza governorate, out of 407 people believed to have been buried there. Among those recovered were 73 children and 106 women. Israel bombs house in Jenin in first strike on West Bank in 10 months: An Israeli military drone struck a house under construction in the Horsh Al-Saada on the western outskirts of Jenin in the occupied West Bank on Friday, as large numbers of Israeli forces entered the area. It marked the first Israeli airstrike on the West Bank in around 10 months. Reporting from the area, Drop Site contributor Mujahed al-Saadi said that the house was struck with at least two missiles and that Israeli troops deployed to the area immediately after the attack, preventing ambulances from reaching the targeted house, and detained Palestinian medical workers who arrived on the scene. Three Palestinians were killed in the strike, according to Reuters. The Israeli military claimed it had carried out a "precise strike" targeting what it described as "several terrorists." Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu the strike on X: "I commend our forces for the successful elimination of the terrorists in Jenin. Shabbat shalom!" Israeli forces raid Nablus; settlers obstruct Friday prayers: Israeli settlers dressed in military uniforms Palestinians from attending Friday prayers at the Al-Wali and Al-Haj Hussein mosques in Beit Furik, east of Nablus, WAFA reported. Separately, Israeli forces the village of Tal, southwest of Nablus, searching homes and detaining one Palestinian and seizing his vehicle. On Thursday, Israeli forces fired sound bombs, tear gassed Palestinians, and sparked fires near homes during a raid on the village of Al-Lubban Asharqiya. Israel detains about 370 Palestinian children, report says: Approximately 370 Palestinian children are imprisoned in Israeli detention centers as of early August, most at Megiddo and Ofer, according to a published on Thursday by the Palestinian Center for Prisoners Advocacy. In the report, children describe Israeli forces raiding their homes at night, taking them away blindfolded and handcuffed, beating and threatening them, and denying them food, water, and bathroom access. During interrogation, children reported experiencing prolonged questioning, isolation, sleep deprivation, and threats against their families. Inside Israeli prisons, they face overcrowding, insufficient food and hygiene supplies, restricted family visits, and delayed or denied medical treatment. Israeli commander says he is "not sorry" for ordering strike that killed seven World Central Kitchen aid workers: Nochi Mendel, who ordered three Israeli drone strikes on the World Central Kitchen (WCK) convoy in Gaza in April 2024, defended his decision to Australia's ABC on Thursday, after he was removed from his post over serious failures and breaches of procedure. Mendel claimed WCK had "ties to Hamas" and was "not really... innocent," although he acknowledged he did not know of those alleged links when he ordered the attack. Israel declined to pursue a criminal investigation against the commander. " Severe food insecurity" in Gaza, according to latest UN figures: In Gaza, 50% of families say they completely ran out of food at least once in the past month and about one in five families say they are eating only one meal a day, according to the latest from the World Food Program (WFP). "Indicators of severe food insecurity remain deeply concerning across the Gaza Strip," the WFP said. Three-quarters of surveyed households reported difficulties accessing food markets. Among them, 96% cited financial constraints related to cash liquidity shortages. Of those able to access money, 40% reported being unable to afford basic food items due to high prices. Nearly half (46%) of surveyed households reported going to bed hungry at least once during the 30 days preceding the survey, with 7% experiencing this more than ten times. Similarly, 50% of households reported completely running out of food at least once during the same period, including 18% who faced this situation more than ten times. Nearly 3% of households reported going an entire day without eating at least once in the past 30 days. The daily average number of trucks crossing into Gaza since last year's ceasefire is 217--far below the 600 trucks per day in the ceasefire agreement that went into effect on October 10, 2025. Iran Iran 's Araghchi: "Putting diplomacy back on track isn't impossible": Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Friday he held "creative discussions" with Qatar's prime minister and foreign minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, saying putting diplomacy back on track "isn't impossible." In a on X, Araghchi said progress hinges on the U.S. understanding that "pressure doesn't work," adding that Washington should "build trust, speak respectfully, acknowledge our rights, and uphold commitments." White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt told Fox News on Thursday that, regarding Iran, Trump "continues to retain all options on the table." "We've had Operation Epic Fury to destroy their military. Now we have Operation Economic Outcast to destroy their economy," Leavitt said, maintaining that there would be no negotiations until Trump feels that the Iranians might "come to the table in a meaningful way." CENTCOM gives updates on blockade, Hormuz: U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) on Thursday that U.S. forces had "redirected 75 commercial vessels, disabled 3, and boarded 2 to ensure compliance" in the Strait of Hormuz. CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper also claimed that U.S. forces had cleared Iranian sea mines from the Strait's internationally recognized shipping lanes, calling it a "major milestone." Cooper added that U.S. forces have overseen the safe passage of nearly 1,500 commercial vessels carrying roughly 750 million barrels of crude through the Strait. Rezaei demands U.S. "fulfill Iran's conditions" to reopen Hormuz, threatens U.S. economic interests if blockade continues: Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei on Thursday that the "U.S. must first take practical steps to fulfill Iran's conditions and then Iran will proceed to open the Strait of Hormuz," according to Iran's Islamic Republic News Agency (IRNA). In a separate interview on Lebanon's Manar TV, Rezaei said Tehran is preparing a list of conditions for reopening Hormuz at the request of mediators. Rezaei said the conditions would include ending the war in the region. Iran has agreed to a transit corridor with Oman, he added, whereby ships would transit through a designated central channel in the strait if the U.S. meets Tehran's conditions. Iran had "fully and transparently" conveyed its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz to Pakistan, which is carrying Tehran's message to Washington, a source told Tasnim on Thursday. Separately, Rezaei on Thursday that Iran would "target U.S. economic interests fully with intensity and force" if the blockade continues, according to state broadcaster IRIB. Rezaei also said that Iran is "closely monitoring the developments related to Beirut and its southern suburbs," adding that those areas are Iran's "red lines." Iran war has depleted Patriot interceptors to "beyond critical" levels: Trump's war with Iran has Patriot interceptor stocks in Europe to "beyond critical" levels, a U.S. defense official and a NATO official told the Associated Press, as European forces use the same air-defense system to protect Gulf oil infrastructure. The Iran war has consumed roughly 1,500 of America's 2,330 Patriot interceptors, or 65% of the stockpile, according to a CSIS estimate. U.S. missiles assigned to Europe have been diverted to the Middle East. A U.S. official said Europe lacks enough Patriots to stop a sustained ballistic-missile attack and has "very limited" capacity against even one strike, warning NATO could be forced to "take punch after punch in the mouth." Trump expected to meet with U.S. oil refiners: Trump is to meet major U.S. refiners and fuel retailers next week as his administration faces mounting pressure over gasoline prices ahead of November's midterms, Reuters reported. Valero, Marathon Petroleum and PBF Energy are among those expected to attend. Trump has previously attacked oil companies benefiting from the price surge. After Exxon and Chevron reported strong second-quarter earnings, he said: "Chevron, too much money. ExxonMobil, too much. Too much money," and called on them to "give some of that back to the public." Yemen Saudi-backed Yemeni government says soldier killed in Taiz: Yemen's internationally recognized government said on Thursday that a soldier in one of its factions had been killed on the Al-Ahtoub front lines in the western countryside of Taiz governorate, as clashes with Ansarallah continue. Lebanon Israeli violations continue across southern Lebanon: Israeli forces Friday toward Aita Al-Jabal in the Bint Jbeil district in southern Lebanon from the occupied town of Hadatha, setting fires on the outskirts, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. On Thursday, Israel three airstrikes on Qantara in the Marjayoun district, while Israeli drones dropped several canisters containing explosives on homes in Mansouri in the Tyre (Sour) district. Israeli forces also white phosphorus near Kfar Roumanne, overnight into Thursday, according to L'Orient. Israel claims Hezbollah launched two explosive drones at troops: The Israeli military Hezbollah launched two "booby-trapped drones" toward Israeli troops operating around the Ali Al-Taher hills overnight Wednesday into Thursday. No casualties were reported. U.S. News Trump signs order renaming Lake Ontario "Lake America" amid Canada trade dispute: President Donald Trump an executive order Thursday directing the renaming of Lake Ontario, which borders New York and Canada, to "Lake America," escalating his trade dispute with Canada, according to NPR. "We have a gulf, and we have a lake, now all we need is an ocean," Trump told reporters at the Oval Office signing, a reference to his earlier renaming of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America, before blaming Canada directly, calling it "the worst to trade" among U.S. partners. The move follows the collapse of trade talks and Trump's imposition of a 50% tariff on some Canadian goods, which prompted Canadian counter-tariffs. Judge again blocks Trump 's mail-in voting order days before ballots ship: U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani implementation of President Donald Trump's executive order limiting mail voting for two weeks Thursday, halting the directive for a second time about a week before the first midterm mail ballots are due to be sent, according to the Associated Press. The ruling came after Democrats and voting rights groups refiled their lawsuits following a Supreme Court decision that let the administration proceed on procedural grounds without ruling on the order's legality. Talwani wrote that plaintiff states "have neither time nor funds" to redesign ballots and update election systems to comply with new Postal Service requirements before the midterms. Fired Stars and Stripes journalists sue Pentagon over dismissals: Three journalists at the federally funded Stars and Stripes news organization the Pentagon on Thursday, alleging their firings came in retaliation for reporting on worsening conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln during its extended nine-month deployment. The lawsuit says the Defense Department moved to fire the reporters a day after Stars and Stripes published an article detailing sailors' food and water shortages, disrupted mail, and poor mental health during the extended deployment. One reporter said his termination notice cited a CBS interview in which he called censorship of news for service members "a red line." Gas industry group boasts of shaping NY Gov. Hochul 's pipeline reversal: Natural Allies for a Clean Energy Future, a public relations group backed by pipeline companies including Williams Companies, told a fossil fuel industry conference in April that it had had "high-level engagement" with Governor Kathy Hochul 's office shortly before she reversed her opposition to new gas pipelines in November 2025, according to industry materials . U.S. negotiating for stake in Venezuela oil fields: The Trump administration is with Venezuela's interim government for a stake in more than a dozen oil fields holding an estimated 90 billion barrels, Axios reported on Thursday, citing two U.S. officials. Officials say the deal could more than double U.S. proven oil reserves. In return, private companies, including American firms, would redevelop Venezuela's aging infrastructure and direct more oil revenue to Caracas. Trump was reportedly considering U.S. ownership of Venezuelan fields before authorizing the January 3 capture of President Nicol as Maduro. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodr iguez are leading the talks, with Stephen Miller also involved. EEOC finds reasonable cause Cisco subjected pro-Palestine workers to hostile workplace: The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission reasonable cause to believe Cisco violated Title VII by subjecting a class of workers to a hostile environment based on Middle Eastern origin, Muslim faith or association with Muslim and Middle Eastern people. An open letter signed by 1,700+ employees urged Cisco to stop supplying technology to Israel's government. The complaint says harassment on Cisco's Inclusive Communities platforms began October 7, 2023, and continued after repeated complaints. It also alleges Cisco fired an employee over pro-Palestine efforts, though the EEOC did not make a separate finding on that claim. . 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News UN envoy registers concern with "open-ended Israeli military presence in Syria": Claudio Cordone, the UN deputy special envoy for Syria, told the UN Security Council that he is "concerned by statements from senior Israeli officials advocating an open-ended Israeli military presence on Syrian territory." He noted that the Israeli presence violates Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity and is inconsistent with the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, adding that Israeli forces have continued military activity in southern Syria, particularly in Quneitra and Yarmouk Basin. Syria 's president appoints former Kurdish SDF commander as advisor: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa has Mazloum Abdi, leader of the now-dissolved Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces, as an advisor to the presidency, state news agency SANA reported. The move comes three days after Abdi announced the SDF's dissolution, following its integration into the Syrian military under a deal struck with Damascus in January. The U.S.-backed SDF had spearheaded the fight against ISIS and was the largest force still outside the Syrian army. Kuwait, Pakistan sign joint defense agreement: Kuwait and Pakistan formalized a joint defense agreement during the visit of the Kuwaiti defense minister to Pakistan on Thursday. The agreement intends to "strengthen operational coordination, exchange military experiences, and enhance the level of readiness and integration" among the armed forces of both countries, according to representatives from the countries. Pakistan's armed forces will assist Kuwait in training and capacity building, according to state-run Pakistan TV, and assist Kuwait with "border management" and "other mutually agreed areas of defense cooperation." Pakistan signed a joint defense agreement with Saudi Arabia and Turkey earlier this month. Nepal-Tibet flood death toll rises to 552: On Friday, Nepal's police announced a new death toll of at least 547 people from Wednesday's floods, while Chinese state media confirmed at least five deaths on the Tibet side, bringing the overall total to 552. 1,924 people remain missing across both sides of the border, including hundreds of foreign nationals, according to a report from Nepal's disaster authority on Friday morning. RSF-SPLM-N forces claim capture of two army bases in Blue Nile fighting: Sudan's Rapid Support Forces Friday its joint force with the Sudan People's Liberation Movement-North captured the Bakori and Surkum army bases in the southeastern Blue Nile region bordering Ethiopia, taking weapons, equipment, and prisoners, according to Sudan Tribune. Separately in South Kordofan state, army forces repelled a dawn RSF assault Friday on the town of Tibsa near Abbasiya Tagali, forcing paramilitary fighters to retreat toward Moreib after several hours of clashes. Two more U.S. deportees arrive in Eswatini under third-country agreement: Two migrants from Latin America deported from the United States in Eswatini on Thursday, the fifth such group sent to the southern African kingdom since July 2025. The Eswatini government did not identify the deportees, disclose their nationalities, or say how long they would remain. The Trump administration has struck third-country deportation agreements with roughly two dozen countries, including about 11 in Africa. Eswatini's King Mswati III has long faced accusations of violently suppressing pro-democracy movements in the country. Jakarta police detain over 300 after protests: Indonesian police more than 300 people, including 160 minors, and named 45 suspects following late-night rioting that erupted after Thursday's anti-government demonstrations near parliament, Reuters reported. Jakarta police accused a group of rioters of setting fire to a police post and two motorcycles and of throwing rocks and sticks at officers. The police used a water cannon and tear gas against the protesters. A man was found unconscious at the scene and later died at a hospital. President Prabowo Subianto's approval rating fell to 38% in a recent Tempo poll over his economic policies. Qatar pledges support for Libyan unity during Benghazi visit : Qatar's Minister of State Mohammed bin Abdulaziz al-Khulaifi with Khalifa Haftar, commander of the eastern-aligned Libyan National Army, in Benghazi, expressing Qatar's support for Libyan sovereignty and "a political process that reflects Libyans' aspirations," according to a Qatari Foreign Ministry. Libya, split since 2014 between the Tripoli-based Government of National Unity and the Haftar-backed eastern administration, reached a new pact last week rewriting election laws and setting a 24-month deadline for elections. Palestine Action activists charged with "terrorism" offenses over Trump golf course protest: Seven Palestine Action activists who spray-painted messages and damaged Trump's Turnberry golf resort in Scotland during a March 2025 protest have been with malicious damage "having a terrorist connection," according to reporting by The Guardian and The New York Times. The activists sprayed red paint on the clubhouse, damaged turf and sprinklers, applied weedkiller to greens, and painted "Gaza is not 4 sale" on the property in protest of Trump's stance on Gaza. The case comes days after the U.S. Treasury Department imposed sanctions on Palestine Action and the pro-Palestine group Masar Badil, along with financial penalties on the Italian digital services group Autistici Inventati. | | ---|---|--- 📖 Do Rural Residents Have the Power to Say No to Data Centers? 🛒 for your Drop News/Not Bombs Hoodie 💬 our Whatsapp Broadcast Channel for the latest reporting, podcasts, and breaking news, delivered directly ⚠️ You can go to your to unsubscribe from the Drop Site Daily newsletter--while still getting the rest of our reporting Become a Drop Site News Paid Subscriber Drop Site News is reader-supported. Right now, an important bill is sitting on a shelf in Washington because Senate leaders refuse to force a vote. The House of Representatives already did its job and passed the SAVE Act. The goal of this bill is simple and clear: **> > Requires Proof of Citizenship:** It stops non-citizens from voting by requiring real proof of U.S. citizenship to register. **> > Cleans Up Voter Lists:** It forces states to clear non-citizens off voter roles. **> > Holds Officials Accountable:** It sets strict penalties for election officials who break the rules. | It's Mary Trump.

Five years ago, after the attack on the Capitol, I said my uncle was unstable and needed to be removed from office immediately.

**_I was right then, and the case is only more clear now._**

I've made this argument as a clinical psychologist, as his niece, and as someone who grew up watching exactly how my family wields power. My opinion as to whether Donald is capable of doing the job of the presidency has never wavered, and the evidence should be even more obvious to anyone willing to look.

Consider what we've all watched recently. Donald calls foreign leaders by the wrong names. He invents countries that don't exist. He cannot stay awake through his own meetings. His hands are bruised, his ankles are swollen, and he has no impulse control. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138103565/642993586/-1632084458?amount=10&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.08.28_Mary-Trump-Split_B1_F1_S1_C1_90OP_N-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODg1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNWQ1ZjVlOC0wMGEzLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=JJy0dutzkUo78gzzI64I4B2w0ERvFQe1nvRYQIk22No=) **Here's the part I most need you to understand: Donald isn't a different person. His cognitive, psychological, and physical decline are simply revealing who he's always been.**

Meanwhile, the people constitutionally empowered to act — his Cabinet, his party — are painfully aware of his unfitness even as they work to cover it up. They have decided that their own hold on power is worth more to them than the country's safety or the rights of the people they purport to serve. They will not act on their own.

**So the responsibility falls to us, and the only real remedy available to us is an electoral one. We are less than three months from Election Day, and what we build between now and then will determine whether this man spends his final two years in office with a Congress that indulges him or one that finally holds him to account.**

That is what Transcend PAC exists to fund. We back candidates who can flip the House, invest in the Senate races that get us to a majority, and put real money into the state races almost nobody is watching.

[**_Will you chip in $10, split between Transcend PAC and Maggie Hassan before our midnight deadline? Folks might've killed to have my job.
I was a sideline reporter for pro football and basketball. I covered some of the most exciting games in history. I watched sports for a living. And I loved every minute, every touchdown, and every Hail Mary.
I reached the pinnacle of my career... but there was one problem:
I had to watch what I said. I was a public-facing representative for a world-class sports network. I couldn't share everything I believed, and no one really knew I was a Conservative.
So I hung up my press badge and quit my dream job so I could speak my mind.

**People said I was OUT OF MY MIND. **
**But I knew God was leading me in a certain direction, and that 's no time for half-measures. I knew he had a plan for my life. So I took a leap of faith and never looked back.**
**[Now, a few years later, I’ve started a growing podcast, campaigned for commonsense in Minnesota, and now launched a campaign for U.S. Senate!](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=8f5bf533d29c4eb8843a1a9571788e12&_e=c6kDtSoeEseyywF70H5xAa5YBfVQ12rwftqjje_JHdDtJgzgOHHW-zc5xDl_Pu_thWkb9rbWY8mYMimzDtJQeIc1EBvhrnYnrCB3nYgXDRmz0Kwd3X-sgv6SwdkwcQOP9FVo5QkQLvvyCTVc-iXpF5fWeO16czrO1mZ8OtSl73aFzX8y1P_VuFRm4KJ-PPPdAixJCLW-C2BuuG6IuNfBfiPZU7XjYClUw5Li7_UUtQKYa-WUpzXPy_eCevVGn9zsuDf_vqA3-2vf8yqcazguE-ntyvDZrA7CkG9bMhuUxgZRN6cQbljJP-jaS1N70Im512CEGasRUxEoP22jt32hLpwk1YZVenk-r4nIQyin8NY02IUAko308SmatZx09cEKih5Ws6N4rtKf8XnYU7PlARwB4_WeMh-WvOGxoLmeVijQzI9hvoVmtD6esgRt1yrA5if8UmMv3WcDmC5kMD3nsXFkwcy_3597n2YzHbcC6hYlpL0Oq-VqW2UerBRN5D3jvM4u2ZeXQHquENjVa1qXwHe7KEOSpIttYs92TWgnBVuFTKSDp8bSEvGYw4v0nT8crokU4gJXjPJPpZmQ52C5F5XRV6njRyASF3lzda_43ijY_oMm72XMFydBYLw2S9RN6BJ-PPgdW6cD08oCH6iYtZy85Tvl5UoN479M2LHqdN2ZvKXH5V8pAfsM9fVNuF0ClgWPSJbrmlPIDMGmFH6L252vhHMW1jLgKrBEW7ehv3MxC-R1SAnSUjuRH0bF3Ygq4cYtLWJ3mq0vyeGgDGwtVrOJSpGsHT7FlyCm-qpaC4Q_ZZNOyHYu1Qhhs1gmNZIYuE9AWdipo0HvFz3_7yb3HQNp69_bqJ6QXJIkzkaqQXw%3D)**
**I believe God put me here for a reason. **
**I believe Minnesota is the land of 10,000 problems right now. **
**And I believe a no-BS, sane person who 's ALL-IN can win this seat. **
**But I 'd be lying if I said fundraising doesn't make a difference in a race like this. The far-Left is readying a FORTUNE to drown out our message and take this seat out of play. **
**Our path to victory solely depends on raising enough to keep up. **
**My finance team tells me we 'll need to bring in donors ASAP so we can: 1) Hire staff, 2) Recruit volunteers in every corner of the state, 3) Print yard signs, 4) Launch our advertising blitz, and 5) Start contacting on-the-fence voters. **

clean_body: This is Michele Tafoya – I’ve got a quick story to share if you’ll indulge me for a few moments. | Hi there, I hope you are well! Folks might've killed to have my job. I was a sideline reporter for pro football and basketball. I covered some of the most exciting games in history. I watched sports for a living. And I loved every minute, every touchdown, and every Hail Mary. I reached the pinnacle of my career... but there was one problem: I had to watch what I said. I was a public-facing representative for a world-class sports network. I couldn't share everything I believed, and no one really knew I was a Conservative. So I hung up my press badge and quit my dream job so I could speak my mind. It was the hardest decision I've ever made. I was scared, excited, and liberated - all at the same time. People said I was OUT OF MY MIND. But I knew God was leading me in a certain direction, and that 's no time for half-measures. I knew he had a plan for my life. So I took a leap of faith and never looked back. I believe God put me here for a reason. I believe Minnesota is the land of 10,000 problems right now. And I believe a no-BS, sane person who 's ALL-IN can win this seat. But I 'd be lying if I said fundraising doesn't make a difference in a race like this. The far-Left is readying a FORTUNE to drown out our message and take this seat out of play. Our path to victory solely depends on raising enough to keep up. My finance team tells me we 'll need to bring in donors ASAP so we can: 1) Hire staff, 2) Recruit volunteers in every corner of the state, 3) Print yard signs, 4) Launch our advertising blitz, and 5) Start contacting on-the-fence voters. I 'm afraid that'll make the difference between a winning campaign and a losing one. | I put my career on hold to speak out for what I know to be true. I 'm committing my blood, sweat, and tears to take this seat back from the political class. I 'd be honored if you'd be willing to stand alongside me. Any type of donations will make a impact on our path to victory. I hope you 'll join us, but either way, God bless you! Be brave. Nvidia posted monstrous quarterly earnings this week, but those results still were **[not enough to drive a breakout](https://substack.com/redirect/5c4de7df-b907-4e15-8c45-7bf0452ceb05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in the broader chip sector on Friday.

---|---|---
* **70% growth still constrained:** Nvidia projected about 70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028 and about $108 billion this quarter after another blowout report.
* **Thursday pop, limited follow-through:** Shares jumped nearly 9% Thursday and added about $440 billion in value, with Broadcom and Intel rising after the release.
* **Demand outruns what it can ship:** CEO Jensen Huang said AI reached its inflection point and demand is much greater than 70%, but supply is the cap.
* **Rivals and shortages linger:** Customer-built custom chips, tight memory supply, and capacity limits at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. remain headwinds.

# [Pentagon labeled Anthropic a threat. A judge said no](https://substack.com/redirect/7118ccfe-25f7-47f3-b954-119b1e7ddc8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A **[San Francisco federal judge](https://substack.com/redirect/af2aa4e0-73e8-4bde-a338-6fd5d8c7699d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on Thursday ruled the Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic as a supply chain risk was illegal, finding the Defense Department violated the First Amendment.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7118ccfe-25f7-47f3-b954-119b1e7ddc8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Retaliation, not national security:** U.S. District Judge Rita Lin found the Department of Defense acted to make a public example of Anthropic, not on an articulable security basis.
* **Claude talks collapsed in March:** Anthropic wanted limits on autonomous weapons and domestic mass surveillance; the Pentagon wanted unfettered access to Claude for all lawful uses.
* **D.C. case keeps the brand marked:** Anthropic still technically remains a supply chain risk until its separate Washington, D.C., lawsuit is resolved.
* **IPO path just got clearer:** The ruling clears a major hurdle as Anthropic heads toward an expected near-record IPO and possible renewed Pentagon work.

# [Warsh goes to Jackson Hole with a message about AI and Inflation](https://substack.com/redirect/7118ccfe-25f7-47f3-b954-119b1e7ddc8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said Friday in Jackson Hole, Wyo., that **[artificial intelligence could turbocharge the economy](https://substack.com/redirect/32dea390-c27c-4927-8a51-498741184dd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and that the central bank is watching its impact closely.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7118ccfe-25f7-47f3-b954-119b1e7ddc8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Capital keeps flooding in:** Warsh said the potential for substantially higher growth is rising as ever-expanding pools of capital pour into AI-related infrastructure of all sorts.
* **New factor of production:** He said the Fed sees AI as a potential new factor of production with consequences for both the economy and interest rates.
* **Models and tokens watched:** The central bank is attentively tracking large language models at the heart of AI and the tokens used to access those models.
* **Jobs task force is live:** A Warsh-appointed task force is weighing when productivity rises, who captures the value, and what that means for workers.

#### Inflation is 3.7%. Warsh says that's not good enough
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said Friday **[at Jackson Hole](https://substack.com/redirect/2fcd6275-ac2d-48b2-9786-6a3128be5481?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that inflation is running too high and **[the central bank has work to do,](https://substack.com/redirect/8eebdea9-3ad9-44a0-9c2f-3b736c32f357?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while offering no forward guidance on rates.
* **Conditions barely look restrictive:** Warsh said he sees little evidence that broad financial conditions are holding the economy back after the Fed kept rates unchanged at all 5 meetings this year.
* **AI lifts capex sharply:** He estimated capital expenditures rose 9% over the past 4 quarters, with more than half of this year's gain likely tied to the AI build-out.
* **Target slips amid war:** Inflation moved further from the 2% goal amid the Iran war, and Warsh said summer PCE and CPI readings still do not signal a real improvement in underlying trends.
* **Households keep spending:** Inflation-adjusted consumer spending rose more than 2% over the past 4 quarters despite a surge in oil prices, tariffs, and other shocks.

# [Advent, Stripe abandon $50 billion PayPal pursuit](https://substack.com/redirect/7118ccfe-25f7-47f3-b954-119b1e7ddc8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A consortium of Advent and Stripe **[abandoned its more than $50 billion pursuit of PayPal,](https://substack.com/redirect/f0a1b327-ba84-4fd8-a824-864def4f21ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** people familiar with the matter said, ending talks that had helped lift the stock.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7118ccfe-25f7-47f3-b954-119b1e7ddc8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Board wanted a higher price:** The Wall Street Journal reported this month that PayPal found the initial bid insufficient and that both sides had been negotiating a higher figure.
* **Takeover premium just vanished:** PayPal shares had jumped more than 40% this quarter to a market value of about $52.6 billion on earnings and deal talk.
* **Stock snapped after the walk-away:** PayPal traded at $54.40, down $7.08 or 11.51%, as of 11:40 AM EDT after the reports hit.
* **Door is not fully closed:** People said the situation is fluid and Advent and Stripe could still return later; Advent, PayPal, and Stripe declined to comment.

# [Costco will now deliver the cake. Yes, that cake](https://substack.com/redirect/7118ccfe-25f7-47f3-b954-119b1e7ddc8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Costco and Instacart said **[shoppers can now order custom sheet cakes,](https://substack.com/redirect/72a899a6-df32-4ed2-9172-965e29690ef6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** 10-inch round cakes, and party platters for delivery through Instacart and SameDay Costco.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7118ccfe-25f7-47f3-b954-119b1e7ddc8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Paper bakery forms are gone:** Those made-to-order bakery and deli items were unavailable online until February, when Costco retired a decades-old warehouse paper-form system.
* **Platters join the delivery menu:** Newly available options also include sandwich platters, shrimp trays, and fruit platters for celebrations that once required a store visit.
* **Design the cake in the app:** Shoppers can choose size, shape, and flavor, pick a preset design, and add a message of up to 30 characters in a chosen color.
* **Nearly 10 years in the making:** Instacart commercial chief Ryan Hamburger said the partnership, which began with same-day delivery in 2017, now covers made-to-order bakery and deli.

Households keep spending: Inflation-adjusted consumer spending rose more than 2% over the past 4 quarters despite a surge in oil prices, tariffs, and other shocks. | | | | ---|---|--- | Aug 16 | A consortium of Advent and Stripe people familiar with the matter said, ending talks that had helped lift the stock. | | ---|---|--- Board wanted a higher price: The Wall Street Journal reported this month that PayPal found the initial bid insufficient and that both sides had been negotiating a higher figure. Takeover premium just vanished: PayPal shares had jumped more than 40% this quarter to a market value of about $52.6 billion on earnings and deal talk. Stock snapped after the walk-away: PayPal traded at $54.40, down $7.08 or 11.51%, as of 11:40 AM EDT after the reports hit. Door is not fully closed: People said the situation is fluid and Advent and Stripe could still return later; Advent, PayPal, and Stripe declined to comment. Costco and Instacart said 10-inch round cakes, and party platters for delivery through Instacart and SameDay Costco. | | ---|---|--- Paper bakery forms are gone: Those made-to-order bakery and deli items were unavailable online until February, when Costco retired a decades-old warehouse paper-form system. Platters join the delivery menu: Newly available options also include sandwich platters, shrimp trays, and fruit platters for celebrations that once required a store visit. Design the cake in the app: Shoppers can choose size, shape, and flavor, pick a preset design, and add a message of up to 30 characters in a chosen color. Nearly 10 years in the making: Instacart commercial chief Ryan Hamburger said the partnership, which began with same-day delivery in 2017, now covers made-to-order bakery and deli. Trump keeps nominating

At every hearing, Senator Blumenthal asks them the simplest question: Was
the United States Capitol attacked on January 6th?

And nominee after nominee dodges it or recites the same script the White
House handed them — because they know the truth doesn't match what Trump
wants them to say.

Senator Blumenthal called them out: “A judge needs to be able to speak
truth to power. That is a basic qualification, and the failure to be able
to speak truth to power is disqualifying.”

He's right. If a nominee can't tell the truth about January 6th and say
the Capitol was attacked, they have no business sitting on the federal
bench.

Trump isn't looking for judges who speak truth to power. He's looking for
loyalists — and he’s stacking the courts with judges who answer to him,
not the Constitution or the truth. Once they're confirmed, we're stuck
with them.

Demand Justice PAC is tracking every one of these hearings. We're calling
out every dodge, every scripted non-answer, every nominee who can't bring
themselves to say what everyone knows happened on January 6th.

Every hearing we expose is one more chance to stop a lifetime loyalist
from reaching the bench — but we can't do it without you.

At every hearing, Senator Blumenthal asks them the simplest question: Was the United States Capitol attacked on January 6th? And nominee after nominee dodges it or recites the same script the White House handed them — because they know the truth doesn't match what Trump wants them to say. Senator Blumenthal called them out: “A judge needs to be able to speak truth to power. That is a basic qualification, and the failure to be able to speak truth to power is disqualifying.” He's right. If a nominee can't tell the truth about January 6th and say the Capitol was attacked, they have no business sitting on the federal bench. Trump isn't looking for judges who speak truth to power. He's looking for loyalists — and he’s stacking the courts with judges who answer to him, not the Constitution or the truth. Once they're confirmed, we're stuck with them. Demand Justice PAC is tracking every one of these hearings. We're calling out every dodge, every scripted non-answer, every nominee who can't bring themselves to say what everyone knows happened on January 6th. body:
Yesterday, Larry Rhoden was endorsed by Donald Trump. But the only endorsement that will ever matter is yours.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/273339371955/health-care-you-deserve-10597913?e=cee7b49c04)

| | | | | | Friend,
Yesterday, Donald Trump gave Larry Rhoden his “complete and total endorsement” for South Dakota governor, a title Rhoden thanked him for within hours.
Yet, that endorsement didn’t come with a plan for our schools, a plan for our family farms, a plan for our ranchers, or a plan for property tax relief.
Too often, politicians chase trophies instead of people. They measure their success by who’s endorsing them in Washington, not by who they’re actually serving here at home.
While South Dakota families are struggling to keep up with rising grocery bills, housing costs, and property taxes, the policies coming out of Washington are making it even harder. Trump is pushing to import more foreign beef, putting additional pressure on our cattle producers, while tariffs raise costs on everyday goods and force working families to stretch their paychecks even further. At a time when South Dakotans need leaders focused on lowering costs and strengthening our local economy, Trump is spending his energy on a new ballroom, renaming bodies of water, and picking fights with Canada.
That is the agenda Larry Rhoden has now chosen to embrace. I’m not chasing anyone’s approval from D.C. While Rhoden was on stage collecting endorsements, I’ve been on the road, from Brule County to Lead. I’ve traveled to every corner of this state to listen to the people who get up at sunup and work until that same sun sets.
The only endorsement that matters is from you. Not from Mar-a-Lago or the Washington elite. From everyday South Dakotans who are tired of leaders looking up the ladder instead of looking out for them.
We have 67 days until November 3rd. Larry Rhoden has Donald Trump in his corner. I intend to have South Dakota in mine.
I ask you to chip in $25, $50, or whatever you can today. This race will be decided by people like you, not by the president.
Forever by your side,Dan Ahlers _Your Candidate for Governor_

name: Nick Begich
subject: What a Month
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alaskans for Nick Begich
body:
This is only the beginning, Alaska | | | | [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/bUSFKr4IUyF?e=6679001ba0&c2id=4b8979688b40abb82eda840804c92b8e)
---
| | | Friend,

**What a month.**

Yesterday, we walked into the first AOGA debate and made the case for Alaska. For the jobs, the energy, and the future that this state has been waiting decades to build. And we won it. Not because of clever lines, but because we had a record to stand on and a vision to point toward.

That win came on the heels of our primary victory, and I want to be clear about something: none of it happened because of me. It happened because of you. Every door you knocked, every call you made, every sign you planted in your yard, every conversation you had with a neighbor. That's what carried us through August. Thank you. I mean that.

**But I'll be honest with you. The job is only beginning.**

We are just over two months out from the November 3rd election. Alaska is finally unlocked. After years of being told "no" by Washington, we are moving toward a self determined future, one where Alaskans decide what happens on Alaska's land and with Alaska's resources. One good term deserves another, and we are not about to hand that progress back.

Because here's what's happening on the other side: the radical socialists and their hand picked candidate, Bill Hill, are pouring millions into Alaska right now. They think they can buy this seat. They think Alaskans can be told what to think.

We know better. But knowing isn't enough. **We have to outwork them.**

Here's what I'm asking of you between now and November 3rd:

• Knock on doors in your neighborhood
• Make phone calls to voters
• Put up a sign, or ten
• Host an event, big or small, in your home or your community
• Write an op ed or a letter to the editor
• Share our message on social media
• Talk to your friends and neighbors about what Team Begich has delivered for Alaska

**Sign up to volunteer here:[www.AlaskansforNickBegich.com/volunteer](https://us.list-manage.com/1CufWjcG_rT?e=6679001ba0&c2id=4b8979688b40abb82eda840804c92b8e)**

Every one of these things matters. Every one of them is something the other side's money can't buy.

Now is the time to double down in the fight for Alaska. **I'm all in. I hope you'll be too.**

For Alaska,
Nick Begich

P.S. If you can only do one thing this week, have one conversation with someone who hasn't made up their mind yet. That's how we win, one Alaskan at a time.
---

I was a sideline reporter for pro football and basketball. I covered some of the most exciting games in history. I watched sports for a living. And I loved every minute, every touchdown, and every Hail Mary.
I reached the pinnacle of my career... but there was one problem:
I had to watch what I said. I was a public-facing representative for a world-class sports network. I couldn't share everything I believed, and no one really knew I was a Conservative.
So I hung up my press badge and quit my dream job so I could speak my mind.

name: John McGuire
subject: Not a politician. A survivor, Peter.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by John McGuire for Virginia
body:
| Peter, I wasn't supposed to make it this far.
Not after foster care. Not after my military service. Not after the day they told my family I wouldn't make it through the night.
But I'm still here. And if you've got 60 seconds, I want to tell you why.
I grew up bouncing between nine elementary schools, no name, no direction, just two grandparents who stepped in when no one else would.
I fought to survive back then. And that fight never really stopped.
At 18, I enlisted. Made it through BUD/S. Became a SEAL. Then a sniper. Then an instructor.
I carried out missions you'll never hear about. Buried teammates you'll never know. Stared evil in the face and pulled the trigger more times than I can count.
But in 2006, it all nearly ended.
A catastrophic injury. A doctor who looked me dead in the eyes and said, "You'll never walk again."
Most men quit at that point. But I didn't have that option. I crawled back, inch by inch, bone by bone. I stood. I walked. I ran. Then I never stopped.
My name is John McGuire.
And I'm not in politics because I wanted a title. I'm in it because I came back from hell and found my country being handed over to cowards.
Because the people trying to erase our history, mock our faith, and dismantle President Trump's legacy want 2026 to be their final victory, and they'll burn the rest of us down to get it.
They told me once I was finished. I didn't accept it then. I won't accept it now.
I know there's a lot out there asking for your attention and your support, Peter.

clean_body: | Peter, I wasn't supposed to make it this far. Not after foster care. Not after my military service. Not after the day they told my family I wouldn't make it through the night. But I'm still here. And if you've got 60 seconds, I want to tell you why. I grew up bouncing between nine elementary schools, no name, no direction, just two grandparents who stepped in when no one else would. I fought to survive back then. And that fight never really stopped. At 18, I enlisted. Made it through BUD/S. Became a SEAL. Then a sniper. Then an instructor. I carried out missions you'll never hear about. Buried teammates you'll never know. Stared evil in the face and pulled the trigger more times than I can count. But in 2006, it all nearly ended. A catastrophic injury. A doctor who looked me dead in the eyes and said, "You'll never walk again." Most men quit at that point. But I didn't have that option. I crawled back, inch by inch, bone by bone. I stood. I walked. I ran. Then I never stopped. My name is John McGuire. And I'm not in politics because I wanted a title. I'm in it because I came back from hell and found my country being handed over to cowards. Because the people trying to erase our history, mock our faith, and dismantle President Trump's legacy want 2026 to be their final victory, and they'll burn the rest of us down to get it. They told me once I was finished. I didn't accept it then. I won't accept it now. I know there's a lot out there asking for your attention and your support, Peter. | | Still here,Congressman John McGuire | Paid for by John McGuire for Virginia John McGuire is a retired member of the United States Navy. subject: Kansas Deserves a Governor Who Keeps Their Word!
body:
| | | | | [](https://natowebbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001t8YKkG8GQ1dkoEEv10DQlCxF0Li-CN3uTuHily-KOJxGH1It19OFliMVRWq8lyOCltwLKPlD0DbmQHZkgPPyPpT6PavE00T-OTo4KvaGG5EehN-K2ma8RaNcqV73LTZLsFY9nrbpzdXfGByjKIuLiaM7qrtR4ViW&c=4c8w0WiWIT06dOwQ2esr2gtBXoi4mSMjPFslqRqxjc_TCv70VkWKhQ==&ch=DX0LTYGKHC8vizYPMWQL1tXcAi3dmKBcth_9LYrzTpZG6kOGkWiESw==)

| Peter,
Radical progressive Cindy Holscher voted AGAINST property tax relief in the Kansas legislature.
I, on the other hand, supported it.
Now, cutting property taxes is one of the central promises of her campaign, but Kansans shouldn't have to guess which Cindy Holscher they're going to get. The candidate who talks about lowering property taxes... or the legislator whose voting record tells a different story?
As Governor, I'll fight to lower property taxes and let Kansas families keep more of the money they work hard to earn. Cindy Holscher has already shown that when given the opportunity, she'll choose bigger government and more spending instead.
Kansas needs a Governor whose record matches their promises, not someone who says one thing on the campaign trail and does another when it's time to vote.
---
| | [](https://natowebbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001t8YKkG8GQ1dkoEEv10DQlCxF0Li-CN3uTuHily-KOJxGH1It19OFlubrmLYJo3mcd_Yn3qmPnYZcXE7DS9lOJwbTEE7Dg5E-t7bnydid8Ik9lUPVTdjsJMxfozjqiYt538to6P1WhJbSoy3fFORUXqChg2sA_LkPoHyEBXbDzSJ8elyreKXQaUFpjoqXZYt2joP5st2bfls=&c=4c8w0WiWIT06dOwQ2esr2gtBXoi4mSMjPFslqRqxjc_TCv70VkWKhQ==&ch=DX0LTYGKHC8vizYPMWQL1tXcAi3dmKBcth_9LYrzTpZG6kOGkWiESw==)

| |

IBEW Local 124 Endorses
---
I'm proud to have the support of IBEW Local 124 and the skilled electrical workers they represent across Kansas.
This marks our third labor union endorsement and is another sign that Kansans across the political spectrum are coming together around a common goal: creating good-paying jobs, strengthening our skilled workforce, and making Kansas a place where people can build a career, raise a family, and prosper.
Our campaign is building a broad coalition because the challenges facing Kansas aren't Republican or Democrat issues. They're Kansas issues.
Thank you to IBEW Local 124 for your confidence and support. I look forward to working together to build a stronger Kansas.
---
|

|

On the Trail with Ty
---
| | Kansas can't have a first-world economy with third-world infrastructure. That's why I sat down with transportation sector business leaders this week in Topeka to discuss how we can improve our state's roads and bridges. As governor, I will work everyday to improve our farmer's and business owner's ability to get their goods to market.

| | | | | [](https://cefuo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001ryrF3LfBD1CfW10NLE-H2MVh-k3SIh01-hOtuvXJfBaW3Q6lIx-SW6SZgEGdQ_0LwqresGk36IcAQDlgOh75RDCbh8j3vvs4TgmGV1Y3cCOmdZGY8J9PQ8E9Mzv-ttxXuJD7RZeO7_xooaChbdEusgr84wJV4uhJlDRBtRKgx7QnTBdRj0L6gw72XEExMwpqALrMHoUXX9ZG6C4LCyTKF-KYMDNEud2MT3B_aWLXH5H61xPjcpKcD490cdNi5xqpO3Q5pWvsqq6nAHI4hi24eYxMQYGyZ1-KhLEAZnxhZyk=&c=Ls7Qs7bPc_hpFZYb55jevLZ85dnlS4_5SCL3HR6oSaEdrJzTeAlbxw==&ch=BEgp_vfgnohwxAkPwRnItQW2vFKdNKp5R-rjoYXL2stGRSgIi8xGSg==)

| My family came to this country because my father was selected through the Diversity Visa Lottery.
That stroke of luck changed the course of our lives, but after we arrived, I watched my parents work multiple jobs, rely on friends for child care and groceries, and fight to build a stable life in an unfamiliar country.
Our community carried us through, but I have never believed that a family's chance to live with dignity should depend on winning a lottery or the kindness of their community.
People should not have to get lucky to find an affordable home, see a doctor, care for their children, earn enough to breathe, or grow old without fear.
Yet that is the economy Congress has allowed powerful corporations and wealthy donors to create. Everything essential has become harder to afford while the people profiting from our struggle keep gaining more influence over our government.
I ran because Denver deserves a representative willing to confront that power directly, and you helped prove that thousands of working people standing together can defeat it.
[Our primary victory was one extraordinary moment in a much longer fight, so will you contribute $26 before our next end-of-month deadline to help us protect this victory, organize for November, and build the progressive power needed to deliver the future we campaigned on?](https://cefuo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001ryrF3LfBD1CfW10NLE-H2MVh-k3SIh01-hOtuvXJfBaW3Q6lIx-SW6SZgEGdQ_0LwqresGk36IcAQDlgOh75RDCbh8j3vvs4TgmGV1Y3cCOmdZGY8J9PQ8E9Mzv-ttxXuJD7RZeO7_xooaChbdEusgr84wJV4uhJlDRBtRKgx7QnTBdRj0L6gw72XEExMwpqALrMHoUXX9ZG6C4LCyTKF-KYMDNEud2MlRt7uSi7D1MHaz-22A1-jA==&c=Ls7Qs7bPc_hpFZYb55jevLZ85dnlS4_5SCL3HR6oSaEdrJzTeAlbxw==&ch=BEgp_vfgnohwxAkPwRnItQW2vFKdNKp5R-rjoYXL2stGRSgIi8xGSg==)
I know what's possible when a community decides nobody will be left to struggle alone. I have seen it in my own family, and I felt it again in every volunteer who knocked on a door, made a call, or trusted this campaign with a contribution.
I am deeply grateful to be in this fight with you. Let's keep going.
Melat

body:
Summer’s coming to an end, but these races are still in a DEAD HEAT. |
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138110544/643014719/1425818251?refcode=WUEFET73_20260828_DHKick_ALL_v1s2&sourceid=1059928&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxYThmZGNiYS0wZWEzLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ycJWnWsBRGXC0zqtRq3yi5uMPAcaG5fCd2Mnz03jehk=) Peter, Yesterday, we launched our Dead Heat Fund with a goal to raise $200,000 for EMILYs List women running in the **_closest_** races of the cycle. These fearless candidates are running to flip the U.S. House, take back power in the U.S. Senate, and win make-or-break state and local elections. [ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

Peter Willis,

Starbucks workers fought for their union — and won. But Starbucks
corporate is still refusing to come to the table, spending YEARS
stonewalling to avoid a contract. Now, the Starbucks union is calling on
all of us to BOYCOTT Starbucks until the company agrees to a first
contract.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39618?source=email-20260828&t=1011&akid=11246%2E5885482%2E2NQC6s ]Headline: Starbucks Workers Union Calls For Boycott Amid Contract Fight

Starbucks made $4.1 billion in profits in 2023. Its new Wall Street-backed
CEO says he wants a “Back to Starbucks” turnaround. Let’s show him what
“back to Starbucks” looks like when Americans refuse to cross the workers’
picket line. Our coffee money won’t go to union-busters.

Every day we hold the line makes it harder for Starbucks to ignore its
workers. We’ve seen it before: when we act together, we win.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39618?source=email-20260828&t=1012&akid=11246%2E5885482%2E2NQC6s ]Will you stand with workers and pledge to boycott Starbucks until the
company sits down and negotiates a fair contract?

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39618?source=email-20260828&t=1013&akid=11246%2E5885482%2E2NQC6s ]ADD YOUR NAME

Since 2021, more than 700 Starbucks stores have voted to unionize. These
workers have been clear: all they want is fair pay, predictable schedules,
affordable health care, and respect on the job.

But Starbucks is stalling. The company drags out endless “negotiation”
meetings, shuts down unionized stores, and tells customers the company is
“making progress” — while refusing to settle even a single contract. Not
ONE of those 700 unionized stores has a contract in place.

It’s no accident. These are tactics right out of the anti-union playbook
that’s become all too common since Trump’s war on workers — giving
companies like Starbucks the green light to ignore the law and block
workers from claiming their rights.

Our Revolution has stood shoulder-to-shoulder with Starbucks workers since
day one — we joined them on the picket lines and in the streets. Now they
need us to show the power of our collective action.

|
#
Major news, friend. **We just won in court against the Trump Administration. ** | **Court ruling threatens GOP cash advantage**
_The case was brought by four Democratic candidates running this cycle — Sen. Jon Ossoff (Ga.), former Sen. Sherrod Brown (Ohio), former Gov. Roy Cooper (N.C.) and Rep. Kristen McDonald Rivet (Mich.)_

In plain English: we just made it harder for MAGA dark money to drown out your voice.
Here in MI-08, national Republicans have been counting on this loophole to stretch their attack ads further. We've already seen $2.5 million reserved against me – and more is sure to come.

body:
I don't usually do this

| Peter,**
**I don't usually do this, but I want to show you something personal today.
I dug up a few old photos – one with my siblings and my single mother, one from my time serving in Afghanistan, and one with my family, long before I set foot in politics.
---
[](https://trk.emails.troydowning.-DsdW5D_bLtgVVUCg)
---
You see, people in Washington think they know my story because they've seen a 30-second ad or interview.
They don't, Peter.
They don't know what it felt like to leave a stable career behind after 9/11, or what it's like to sit in a helicopter over hostile territory, hoping you make it back with the soldier you came for.
I'm sharing these photos because I think you deserve to actually know who’s reaching out with these emails – not just a name on a donation page.
And with the threat of losing our House Majority looming over our heads, I’m counting on every Patriot’s support before November.
[If this story means something to you, I'd be grateful if you could chip in $5, $10, or $15 towards my campaign today.](https://trk.emails.troydowning.)
---

Hi friends, this is deeply concerning to me: **The AP is reporting that ICE has detained or deported more than 50 spouses and parents of active-duty U.S. service members. ** At least six have already been deported, one individual self-deported, and at least eight immediate family members remain in federal immigration detention right now — while their loved ones serve this country in uniform. And just this past weekend, Border Patrol [arrested](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138113009/643022766/1289743956?refcode=260828em_sjj_ice-sm&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ODI3OGExNC0xM2EzLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=zMhLXz-DGLUUifsbp8hSEJRAZTrQsRt6DXRKDtXlEJo=&emci=65278a14-13a3-f111-9b33-0022482a9a8d&emdi=68278a14-13a3-f111-9b33-0022482a9a8d&ceid=14239920) the father of a sailor on the USS Abraham Lincoln, which has reportedly faced deteriorating conditions from food shortages to lack of access to mental health care leading to some service members attempting to [jump overboard](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138113010/643022767/1961527739?refcode=260828em_sjj_ice-sm&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ODI3OGExNC0xM2EzLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=zMhLXz-DGLUUifsbp8hSEJRAZTrQsRt6DXRKDtXlEJo=&emci=65278a14-13a3-f111-9b33-0022482a9a8d&emdi=68278a14-13a3-f111-9b33-0022482a9a8d&ceid=14239920). For decades, under bipartisan consensus, family members of U.S. service members have been protected from deportation. But this administration has rolled back those immigration protections to further its mass deportation agenda (while still promoting these benefits to prospective recruits right now — yes, really). And our military families are paying the price. I represent the largest military community in the country, and I'm the only San Diego member on the House Armed Services Committee. I hear directly from service members and military families about their struggles every single day. _And I take it personally when this administration treats my constituents with disrespect._ How can our service members focus on their jobs while their loved ones are being ripped away from them? Some have been forced to take leave or delay deployment because ICE arrested their spouse or parent and left them with no one to care for their children. This undermines military readiness. It undermines our national security. **And it is deeply, profoundly unpatriotic.** This is the same administration that sent thousands of San Diego sailors and Marines into harm's way in Iran — our neighbors, our friends, people we see at the grocery store and on the sidewalk. They sacrifice their bodies, their mental health, their time with their families, and sometimes their lives for this country. The least we can do is make sure their loved ones are safe while they're gone. **This administration has shown us again and again that they don't give a damn about our service members. I do. clean_body: Disgraceful.| | | | = Hi friends, this is deeply concerning to me: The AP is reporting that ICE has detained or deported more than 50 spouses and parents of active-duty U.S. service members. At least six have already been deported, one individual self-deported, and at least eight immediate family members remain in federal immigration detention right now — while their loved ones serve this country in uniform. And just this past weekend, Border Patrol the father of a sailor on the USS Abraham Lincoln, which has reportedly faced deteriorating conditions from food shortages to lack of access to mental health care leading to some service members attempting to . For decades, under bipartisan consensus, family members of U.S. service members have been protected from deportation. But this administration has rolled back those immigration protections to further its mass deportation agenda (while still promoting these benefits to prospective recruits right now — yes, really). And our military families are paying the price. I represent the largest military community in the country, and I'm the only San Diego member on the House Armed Services Committee. I hear directly from service members and military families about their struggles every single day. And I take it personally when this administration treats my constituents with disrespect. How can our service members focus on their jobs while their loved ones are being ripped away from them? Some have been forced to take leave or delay deployment because ICE arrested their spouse or parent and left them with no one to care for their children. This undermines military readiness. It undermines our national security. And it is deeply, profoundly unpatriotic. This is the same administration that sent thousands of San Diego sailors and Marines into harm's way in Iran — our neighbors, our friends, people we see at the grocery store and on the sidewalk. They sacrifice their bodies, their mental health, their time with their families, and sometimes their lives for this country. The least we can do is make sure their loved ones are safe while they're gone. This administration has shown us again and again that they don't give a damn about our service members. I do. Friend, **_Let’s look at what’s happening to farmerss across Tennessee. _** Our cattle producers are taking _hit after hit_ right now. Between the climbing price of feed, fuel, and proprietary heavy equipment, independent ranchers are already fighting an uphill battle just to keep the lights on. Then, you have federal trade policies pushed by Donald Trump, and cheerleaded by Senator Marsha Blackburn that open the door to cheap foreign beef, directly undercutting the hard work of domestic producers. _**Where is Marsha Blackburn while our agricultural community deals with this?**_ She’s too busy _falling right in line with party leadership_ , and too _lost in her own world of childish culture wars_ to notice that Tennessee's family farms are taking the brunt of these bad and completely avoidable decisions. **As Jerri says,_“You don’t put America first by putting U.S. cattle producers last.”_** Farmers don't need politicians who only show up in rural counties for a photo-op and then fly back to Washington. They need someone willing to stand up and push back against bad trade deals and the corporate costs threatening their livelihood. Tennessee deserves a leader that will work with our farmers to find solutions to support and sustain our agricutural sector.
### **Jerri will _ Fght for Tennessee Farmers_**
* **Protect local cattlemen:** Push back against federal policies that flood our markets with cheap foreign beef.
* **Lower operating costs:** Take on the corporate price-gouging driving up the price of feed and heavy equipment.
* **Reinvest in rural communities:** Fully fund local schools and expand Medicaid so small towns have the support they deserve.

The Denver school tax question says $44 million. The measure says something larger.
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends!
Want your full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** Jewish leaders [want Kiros to address antisemitism concerns](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.); Colorado gets [$615 million from a Meta teen-safety settlement](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.); a former aide [sued three House Democratic leaders](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) over alleged retaliation; Colorado joined 25 states suing USPS over [new citizen-verified mail-ballot rules](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.); Douglas County put a [$54 million tax override on the ballot](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.); and RMV found [Denver's "$44 million" tax question](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) actually authorizes an uncapped jump to 29% of program funding.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** C. J. Garbo argues conservatives need institution-building, [citing RMV as the solution](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.); Greg Walcher examines the [new Colorado River plan](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), which cuts Lower Basin use and forces those states to finally share shortages from their own overuse.
This is your Mountain Minute for Friday, August 28, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[The Denver school tax question says $44 million. The measure says something larger.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
The question Denver voters will mark this November asks whether to raise Denver Public Schools taxes “up to $44 million.” That is the number on the ballot, the number in the district’s public materials, and the figure repeated in news coverage of the measure.
The $44 million is not a fixed cap on what the tax could raise in the years after.
Read the board’s resolution, adopted Aug. 13, along with the ballot question it certified, and the $44 million turns out to be an estimate for the first year.
What voters would also authorize is a permanent change to the ceiling on how much the district can collect through its operational overrides — a ceiling written as a share of the district’s total program funding, not as a dollar figure. The dollar amount it allows moves with that funding rather than holding at $44 million. And the percentage mechanism that sets it appears nowhere in the question.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Stop complaining about the media. Build one — Colorado conservatives already are.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY C. J. GARBO, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_C. J. Garbo argues Colorado conservatives' real challenge isn't winning the next election — it's building the institutions that shape voters' minds long before they ever reach the ballot._
* **Institutions, not just campaigns, win the long game:** Garbo argues conservatives have long focused on winning elections while neglecting the durable institutions — media, advocacy networks, research centers — that shape public opinion between election cycles, and that Rocky Mountain Voice represents exactly this kind of missing civic infrastructure.
* **Scale backed by real numbers:** RMV reaches roughly 200,000 people via email, published over 800 original articles from 98 writers in 2025, and generated 12.5 million social media views — growth Garbo frames not as vanity metrics but as genuine political capacity, since "political pressure comes from numbers."
* **Credibility over propaganda:** Garbo insists the goal can't be building a conservative mirror of biased journalism — RMV must hold conservatives accountable too, correct its own errors, and let facts remain sovereign over perspective, arguing that's the only way such an outlet earns lasting trust with persuadable, unaffiliated voters.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

******[A socialist endorsement for mayor: What Denver DSA’s backing of Shontel Lewis means.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY SHAINA COLE | LOCAL | AUGUST 26** _Denver’s Democratic Socialists of America chapter has picked a candidate in the 2027 race for mayor. In an August 25 release, the chapter said it was “proud to announce their endorsement of Councilwoman Shontel M. Lewis for Mayor of Denver in the 2027 election."_
____
__******[What the Supreme Court did, and did not do, on Trump’s mail-ballot order](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY SHAINA COLE | NATIONAL | AUGUST 25** _The Supreme Court handed the Trump administration a win Monday on mail-in voting, and the headlines said so. But for a Colorado voter, nothing has changed yet. The state remains set to send November ballots under existing rules, because a second court order the justices did not touch still blocks the part of the president’s plan most directly tied to how voters receive their ballots._
**[Three federal cases test whether Colorado treats gun rights as policy or as a limit on government](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY C. J. GARBO | COMMENTARY | AUGUST 25** _Colorado has spent more than a generation treating the Second Amendment as a public-policy question. That is the first mistake. The Bill of Rights does not identify subjects upon which government may act whenever legislators believe their intentions are sufficiently benevolent._**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**__

They're not even hiding it anymore. This is a direct attack on our democracy. **On Monday, the Supreme Court allowed Donald Trump to proceed with his effort to seize control of who gets to vote by mail.** The good news is a U.S. District Judge blocked Trump’s plan to let the federal government dictate who receives a mail-in ballot, and even weaponize the United States Postal Service to decide whose vote gets delivered. But the Trump administration is likely working to appeal the reversal _as we speak._ [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138114178/643026487/2105508926?refcode=ea.a62bafbf-16a3-f111-9b33-0022482a9a8d&ms=ea.a62bafbf-16a3-f111-9b33-0022482a9a8d&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImE2MmJhZmJmLTE2YTMtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMjI0ODJhOWE4ZCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=jb9I2aiTdR_dNvwajksoHNCBhHwm8_QMdb4icbfpzlc=) Trump and his allies know they can't win a fair fight, so they're doing everything they can to rig the rules before Election Day even arrives. **Our answer has to be just as determined. TO: U.S. Postal Service

Dear USPS,

**I am writing today to DEMAND that you stand up to Donald Trump and PROTECT vote-by-mail.**

Vote-by-mail has expanded voting access to millions of Americans in rural areas, serving overseas, and in marginalized communities.

Limiting access to states who do Trump’s bidding is UNDEMOCRATIC and straight up AUTHORITARIAN!

---
Friend,
Today is National Black Giving Day — a day to support Black-led organizations, which are often underfunded, receiving only 1-2% of philanthropic funding. For years I’ve been honored to work with Detroit Justice Center, a thought partner on my policies to reduce mass incarceration and bring about racial justice. A national organization deeply rooted in Detroit, Detroit Justice Center is building equitable cities where everyone thrives — including providing essential legal support for formerly incarcerated people who are seeking to start businesses, worker-owned co-ops led by Black women and other women of color, and community land trusts that provide permanently affordable housing. This badass Black-led organization provides free legal services to keep people out of jail, out of poverty, and in their homes. As a thought partner, Detroit Justice Center uplifts the needs of currently and formerly incarcerated people — helping shape my policies to:
* advance housing justice, including removing barriers to housing for people with criminal records, who are 13x more likely to be unhoused
* push back against the unjust cash bail system and the debt-to-jail pipeline that keeps people locked in cycles of poverty
* shift public funds to community needs rather than state violence
* ensure access to body camera footage without financial barriers

As a former movement lawyer, I’m inspired by Detroit Justice Center’s lawyers who represent protesters, such as anti-war students and people impacted by police brutality — and successfully get their charges dismissed.
The group also provides legal support to formerly incarcerated people who are seeking to start businesses, as well as tenants’ unions and people who are pursuing economic models that put people over profit.
Detroit Justice Center has established 6 community land trusts for permanently affordable housing and 12 worker-owned cooperatives led by Black women and women of color, including a childcare collective, green grocer, and mobile wellness hub.
The group has helped thousands of Michiganders clear the hurdle of suspended licenses, which can spiral into lost jobs and mounting court debt. And now they’re spreading this program to other states.
They’re also collaborating with groups across the country to expand community-led approaches to harm that prioritize healing and accountability over punishment.

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: CVS, CVS, CVS, and CVS.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY WARREN FOR SENATE**
body:
One giant company is usually in charge of the whole supply chain.
#
Imagine you wake up with a headache.
It’s a fairly common experience (especially these days), and one that shouldn’t accidentally put you in the middle of a web of corporate greed.
But it does.
Let's say you go to the doctor. And it's Oak Street Health because that’s close by. Well, Oak Street Health is _**owned**_ by CVS. That’s right — your doctor is owned by CVS.
And let’s say that doctor prescribes you medicine. So you go to your pharmacy, CVS.
That medicine is covered by your insurance, Aetna. And who owns Aetna? Right again, CVS.
But wait, there's a middleman between your pharmacy and insurance company that helps you negotiate prices to lower costs: CVS Caremark. Who owns the middleman? You got it — CVS.
CVS may own your pharmacy. CVS may own your doctor. CVS may own your insurance company. CVS may own the middleman between your insurance company and your pharmacy. One giant company is in charge of the whole supply chain, and you better believe they are taking a cut every step of the way. That means prices get higher and higher, and patients are left paying more and more.
**To fix our country’s inflating health care crisis, we have to break up big medicine once and for all. By doing that, we will lower health care costs for you and your family. And I have a bipartisan bill to get that done.**
**[Add your name today to be a grassroots co-sponsor of the Break Up Big Medicine Act. Together, we can show Congress that Americans are tired of paying more for worse care.](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22967?t=1&akid=1707%2E2118727%2E-3m1Xt)**
**[ADD MY NAME ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22967?t=2&akid=1707%2E2118727%2E-3m1Xt)**
Look, it’s not just CVS.
If you use United Health Group for insurance, you may have had to deal with a pharmacy benefit manager called Optum RX, which is supposed to negotiate prescription drug benefits and decide which drugs are covered by United.
Guess who owns Optum RX? United Health Group. They also own Optum, which is a health services company.
Just as health care prices are set to spike this year following Trump's Big, Ugly Bill, this corporate consolidation ensures that a handful of companies are set up to profit even more.
When our bipartisan bill becomes law, companies that operate as one giant health conglomerate and violate the rules must comply within a year, and regulators, state attorneys general, and even private citizens can take action to enforce the rules.
For decades, policies have encouraged these mega-mergers, letting companies stack the deck to maximize profits while Americans pay more for worse care. We’re finally taking steps to level the playing field.
[**Add your name today to be a grassroots co-sponsor of the Break Up Big Medicine Act.**](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22967?t=3&akid=1707%2E2118727%2E-3m1Xt)
Thanks for being a part of this,
Elizabeth

Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold.
Families were being torn apart.
Lives were being destroyed. **I couldn't forget it.** **I couldn't stay silent.** I kept asking myself one question: **"What if it were my child?"** That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film _Sound of Freedom_. **Not for fame.**
**Not for awards.**
**But because I believed people needed to see the truth.** For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up. **But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.** And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**. Our mission is simple: **To stop the sale of God's children.**

Every day, vulnerable children are targeted by traffickers who prey on poverty, instability, loneliness, and fear. And every day, we work to fight back.
