# **Ninth Circuit just called prediction markets what they are: sports bets**
The Ninth Circuit just smashed the prediction-market costume. Sports event contracts are not swaps, they are sports bets, and Nevada can treat them that way. That slams the Third Circuit's April ruling that handed the CFTC the sandbox. Circuit split. SCOTUS is now the referee. DraftKings jumped 7% because the Street smelled blood.
• **Winners?** DraftKings and Flutter, up 7% and more than 6%. State gaming boards just got a federal blessing. Licensed books get air while the lawyers feast.
• **Losers?** Kalshi, Crypto.com, and Robinhood. Their "it's a derivative, officer" pitch just got laughed out of San Francisco. Forty-four states are circling the rake.
• **Next?** The petition goes to the Supreme Court. Years of fog. Platforms keep running where they can. States keep issuing shutdown orders. Valuation haircuts incoming.
Don't confuse a legal costume with a business. If your volume is football tickets, you are a bookie wearing a CFTC mask. The market already voted: DKNG and FLUT ripped higher on the ruling. The house wins when Washington and the states fight over the juice. Trade the split. Don't marry the narrative.

# **Walmart settles the DOJ opioid case and the stock barely shrugs**
Walmart just settled the Justice Department's 2020 opioid lawsuit and hid the check. That's the tell. If the number was lethal, Bentonville would still be in court. Shares rose 0.5% because this was mop-up, not a body blow. They already paid $3.1 billion to states and cities in 2022. The federal leftover just got swept off the 10-K.
• **Winners?** Walmart. Cloud off the balance sheet, pharmacies keep running, and a 0.5% pop says the Street already priced the pain.
• **Losers?** The 905,000 dead from 1999 to 2025 and a DOJ that wanted billions in penalties then took a secret handshake.
• **Next?** The dollar figure leaks within weeks. Other chains study the template. The epidemic is now a legal product, not a Sunday sermon.
When the biggest retailer on earth settles and the stock yawns up half a percent, the real trial already happened in 2022. This was the federal afterparty. Capitalists settle when fighting's option value goes negative. Walmart did the math. Lawyers got paid. America still has a pharmacy problem. Trade the stock, not the eulogy. Its a brutal reality.

# **Affirm surges as $4.09 gas turns shoppers into installment addicts**
Max Levchin just showed you the inflation trade live. Affirm printed Q4 revenue of $1.17 billion against a $1.11 billion LSEG number, GMV hit $14.1 billion versus $13.39 billion, and fiscal Q1 guidance of $1.19 billion to $1.22 billion beat the $1.16 billion Street print. The stock surged. Gas sits at $4.09. Broke people budget. Affirm collects.
• **Winners?** Affirm and Levchin. Sticky 3.7% inflation is their customer-acquisition machine. Households stretching $4.09 gas across installments are the inventory.
• **Losers?** The U.S. consumer eating $4.09 gas, still far above pre-Iran-war levels. Card networks losing the "budgeting" customer straight to Buy Now Pay Later.
• **Next?** Warsh's September Fed meeting. If prices stay sticky, Affirm keeps printing. If the pump cracks, that "budgeting" bid cools fast.
Levchin said the quiet part: when inflation bites, demand for his product goes up. That is not a health report. That is a toll booth on American weakness. Ride AFRM while $4 gas and 3.7% inflation keep the installment machine humming. Do not confuse their beat with a healthy shopper. Parasites love a squeeze.

# **Gen Z just pawned the 401(k) to the sportsbook**
Betterment surveyed 1,000 investors and 52% of Gen Z, born 1997 to 2007, already yanked money meant for investing and fed it to a sportsbook. A quarter of them think a parlay is a retirement plan. The vig is $110 to win $100. The stock market compounded around 10% for a century. These kids are torching the engine.
• **Winners?** DraftKings, FanDuel, and every book skimming the juice. Platforms are harvesting a generation that treats gambling like an asset class.
• **Losers?** Gen Z's future net worth. I already called this long-term suicide for compounding in **["Gen Z torches their American dream by abandoning marriage forever."](https://substack.com/redirect/d9c36447-5b88-48aa-ba0a-2057179de938?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
• **Next?** Delinquency and bankruptcies keep climbing, exactly as the New York Fed already mapped. The books keep the rake. The kids keep the debt.
I told you these kids were committing long-term suicide for compounding. Here is the receipt. 52% redirected investment money. Sports bettors already miss bills at a 25% clip and 30% take on debt. Ten grand in the index becomes $452,000 in 40 years. A Sunday ticket becomes a bar story. The house cashes it.

By Illinois Review

Lyons Township Clerk Elyse Hoffenberg released surveillance footage Thursday night showing her after-hours kiss with Bridgeview Mayor Steven Landek — and the video is now raising new questions about how she previously characterized the encounter.

Hoffenberg, who is married and is the Democratic candidate for Cook County Board District 17, had described the July incident as a “peck” and told Patch that she immediately told Landek the contact was “inappropriate” and that Landek apologized.

But the newly released footage provides a fuller picture of the encounter.

Hey there Fellow Patriot,

It’s Jackie Mary Auringer, a Hudson Valley native running for Congress in New York's 18th District to raise up the place that raised me.

My parents dedicated their lives to this community, my mother as a teacher and my father as a local business owner. They raised me to believe in responsibility, accountability, and pride in where you come from. Those are the values I am bringing to this race every single day.

**[But Fellow Patriot, I have to be honest with you about what we are up against.](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=e44ad0aea16c42808ca8e5bd29d2a9c2&_e=kPv6kenYE0WhlpiB07h7h92tgX7pRFLEPX_OjJzwy8K6B6Vv84OKhsjsAi_VT5x9WdfRNj2MPN5q6SF9AFmYQtgallVDKI4w0TFxEB3JWAQ1OrZA1fee-yg2XMMLsJewLoSl0G4e1TP2lJr8E3rqmcIbu4bgsnNcfpWw6DDnRdi8ZUp3ZI2uicO3gLa6Kk-0peOlWAz5TJAauOuQDFHYYp2eDf0f-knqlu1WjLl_MRRdAFZGO6q83oUQPsWIrQnHTfzwSq9SiGOFN8ow08n1iOHFlotdH6_jl5bIZuA_ZjN1OiV9FKG8DKQ_6ArBo2XqoWG72uJGhta8m-aQ2MM_3N_QCfdNehy4sJJ2VkVLjM4Q-wHZsmM6ejY93WaT616M2e9kwJHnOIrDLM-sgCiVK-v7XD4nnLdGWap0pz_YifAIjqOUTgXIsZvWrvCphTvuPy-BPiFFO1sdixsWTBjTMK3Pfu1wXBoyb2SDlASe7Hffvx7kXLHMbEq1q1e_iuEzyc9bqmuBXs-C0aCEsd64L41Ad8Eq_ZSWLsl3r5NqFQhvgpPeWXisf47xi-bjzsS5A8TC-SXM7UcYHoFxodVt7l2sf9v_nLihGL_nqwMp_AR89j-_1nLPmJXDDM-aOIH_Vh0WGK9qJKSWzHpoIr2VzWEkqAaX1mpuX2F0quSoWjYwet3s1_6-NhUqIa5uWfjpeoCy23zkg-HtI-r6CJktTuJUeIf-KKw3kd0RZbXJrLe7Hz0ctDKZFF9dropLvDHo-31yhbu5-as_00txL1O-rg%3D%3D)**

Radical socialists just swept Democratic primaries across New York and Michigan. A brand new CBS poll found that 58% of Democrats now view socialism more favorably than capitalism. And my opponent Pat Ryan is endorsed by the Working Families Party, the same party driving this socialist wave across our state.

5-minute read · 4 stories
Lead Story · Election IntegrityFEDERAL JUDGE BLOCKS TRUMP'S MAIL-BALLOT RULE ONE WEEK BEFORE BALLOTS GO OUTWhat's Happening
* U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani, an Obama appointee, issued a **14-day temporary restraining order** Thursday blocking enforcement of the Postal Service's newly finalized mail-in voting rule.
* The 11-page order halts the provisions mandating ballot-envelope standards, requiring states to enroll voter data on a USPS federal ballot portal, and barring states from mailing ballots to voters who don't comply.
* Talwani wrote that plaintiff states have "neither time nor funds to design new mail ballots, seek approval of the new designs, order production of mail ballots, update their own election management systems, train election officials to use the USPS portal and upload citizen data to the portal, all before the midterms."
* She also found a "significant risk of disenfranchisement" and said the balance of harms and public interest warranted the order.
* **24 states and Washington, D.C.** brought the suit. A hearing is set for **Sept. 3** , and the order covers all Nov. 3 elections for now.

The Situation
* The rule implements Trump's March executive order on citizenship verification and election integrity. Talwani blocked parts of it in July; the Supreme Court set that ruling aside earlier this week on procedural grounds only — it did not rule on whether the order is lawful.
* Once USPS finalized the regulation this week, the states refiled — which is what put the question back in front of Talwani.
* USPS has said it will refuse outbound mail ballots from states that don't submit recipient information through its portal and meet the envelope and barcode requirements.
* Roughly one in three American voters casts a mail ballot. A 2025 Brookings Institution study put documented mail-ballot fraud in 2016–2022 general elections at about **four cases per 10 million ballots**. Both figures are worth holding in mind: the volume is enormous, and proven fraud in the existing system has been rare.
* An appeal is expected quickly and the case could reach the Supreme Court again before ballots are mailed.

The PerspectiveRequiring that a mail ballot be verifiably sent to a real, eligible citizen is not a radical idea, and conservatives are right that a system handling tens of millions of ballots should be auditable. But the timing here is the administration's own doing. Finalizing a rule that rebuilds ballot design, state data systems, and poll-worker training barely two months before Election Day invited exactly this injunction — and a judge blocking a rule on grounds that states physically cannot comply in time is not the same as a court blessing loose elections. If the White House wants durable reform rather than a headline, it should win these fights in the off-year, in statute, with lead time. Reforms rushed into a midterm get struck down; reforms built to last get implemented.[Read the full story at Fox News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_NRx3TmKyUjNZ_2a-If6mrekz44zb6bbBgtpCKJLUBfxCkGZbPjw8mCORidpFN9BvIa8IA6Hs2fynMNTG16cfqTfGb6Ama8hWeyz992KA8WiEN-pwh1MuCeW_X_jwOOtwKD5MZYWQ4663xqr7YD54JZnqQUkwISS44_UAjy76WUrv0KiUzSEP1MJbnANBh5RXaMtJSqhbRjMarR9KmaLquZciruQPnFd7Ox1tbRlzX7wQfF3xHT1ulshz-gey1l4LxyLSp294KpkG-vMwTn3c9sUvAspniFYCj0GPSH2-oZ4hFCpFgJawp2SpC2MjCky2Z9yv2uQsIiLWoVKGvhhHrc/4tk/s6Jl3zsORIWsPMciKRaZYg/h1/h001.27ZHgebCUh_azc8-YmU6db5Wfsg7eHVqa4UXNmNemYM)

The EconomyDEBT HITS $40 TRILLION AS FISCAL HAWKS REJECT BESSENT'S "GROW OUR WAY OUT" MATHWhat's Happening
* The national debt crossed **$40 trillion** last week, pushing yields on long-term Treasury securities to multiyear highs.
* Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said there is "nothing magic" about the milestone and that the government "can grow our way out of that."
* Brett Loper of the Peter G. Peterson Foundation countered that doing so would take "gangbusters 4.3% growth every single year," which he called "all but unattainable." The economy grew **2.1%** last year and **2.8%** the year before.
* Treasury confirmed this month a **$1.8 trillion deficit** over the first 10 months of fiscal 2026.
* Former Speaker Paul Ryan: "You have to keep your nominal GDP growing ahead of your servicing costs, so that you can stabilize the debt ... but you can't grow your way out of total debt reduction," adding that Social Security and Medicare reform is unavoidable — "There's no getting around that."

The Situation
* CBO, the Federal Reserve, and the Blue Chip forecaster survey all project annual growth at or below 2% for the next decade — meaning growth would have to roughly double for Bessent's math to work.
* The debt first crossed $1 trillion in 1981. The last balanced budgets ran from fiscal 1998 through fiscal 2001.
* Former Rep. Carolyn Bourdeaux (D-GA), now at the Concord Coalition: "There's zero chance we're going to be able to grow our way out of this right now, given the current deficits that we run."
* Caleb Quakenbush of the Bipartisan Policy Center noted the last comparable debt load came right after World War II, but that an aging population now pressures entitlements, with AI's effect on long-run growth "a huge question mark."

The PerspectiveGrowth is necessary and it is not sufficient — and the people saying so loudest here are Republicans, not the left. Paul Ryan and the Peterson crowd are making the case fiscal conservatives have made for thirty years: you cannot outrun compound interest on $40 trillion at multiyear-high yields while spending keeps climbing. A $1.8 trillion deficit in ten months is not a growth problem, it's a spending problem, and pretending otherwise from the Treasury podium sets up the next administration to inherit a bill nobody can pay. Conservatives should hold their own side to the standard they'd apply to Democrats: name the cuts, reform the entitlement math, and stop treating a $40 trillion milestone as a rounding error.[Read the full story at Washington Examiner](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_F0KAElx4yVoiF03sTMUTyWslDrlWqxLOtIy7S3gUPIASD0ELcOiJzMJMqpPrZwVoyuyIinQ4462uqpEhJinqit9rWfIQPp8aqld6LWz-YE-SHzi022dDfmptDDTE35HYIl7MQQmz2f3t-DPii48_4XNJ-8xYHTvBWzcd5hPFM0eLx1K135rlcpy00rCgK3yPbkzRh2Sjtw_XmcVecjWa-Z9c6s9rHjL8IUcr79haesG00dlqv0i2V6XcPcFkiBtFC_xOk9vpaglcVsiEnf0X3DXNYKc9xCMDk-sQKPUZiVgspRl5v5CVAiWtrPJWKKNNKvqA-vbZSc-GRtuTPZWqYfmM9SP-A-GoHZBrqOB5zRjanJwofRy4WoHMcAeL4xvicWxnGvYC3srZCmJ5PuzLVI/4tk/s6Jl3zsORIWsPMciKRaZYg/h2/h001.Z23mBnXM89hTqBFuo90dwBYYwyhIs2VfbeHM8gZhLDQ)

Foreign PolicyIRAN AND OMAN AGREE ON A HORMUZ SHIPPING CORRIDOR — BUT TEHRAN WANTS U.S. CONCESSIONS FIRSTWhat's Happening
* Iran and Oman have reached an understanding on a **temporary two-way shipping corridor** through the Strait of Hormuz, but Tehran says it will not implement the arrangement without U.S. concessions.
* Per Iran's defense-linked Defa Press outlet, the inbound route into the Persian Gulf would run **entirely through Iranian waters**. These details come from Iranian state-aligned media and have not been independently confirmed.
* Iran ties implementation to four demands it says were in a June memorandum of understanding: lift the naval blockade of Iranian ports and vessels, release frozen assets, impose no new sanctions, and halt further U.S. military escalation.
* Tehran wants any American steps to be "visible and verifiable" before it acts.
* Under the plan, the southern route through Omani waters that the U.S. has urged ships to use would eventually close. Iranian officials estimate **30 to 60 days** to negotiate a permanent replacement system.

The Situation
* The strait does not reopen on this news. The agreement is contingent, and the Washington Examiner reported it sought White House comment.
* The administration has shifted in recent weeks toward economic strangulation — expanded sanctions plus threats against countries and companies still trading with Iran — rather than new strikes.
* Axios reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio told foreign counterparts the U.S. plans to refrain from striking Iran until after the midterms. That is a single-outlet report attributed to unnamed officials, not a confirmed policy.
* Higher gas prices tied to the conflict have been a persistent political liability heading into November.

The PerspectiveRead the fine print before anyone calls this a breakthrough. Iran is offering to unblock a waterway it had no right to close, and asking in exchange for its assets back, its blockade lifted, and a promise of no new sanctions — with the new inbound lane routed through its own territorial waters, where it controls the traffic. That is not a concession; it is a toll booth. The pressure campaign is working precisely because Tehran now wants something, and the answer to a regime bargaining with other nations' commerce is to keep the leverage and demand verifiable steps first. She also found a "significant risk of disenfranchisement" and said the balance of harms and public interest warranted the order. 24 states and Washington, D.C. brought the suit. USPS has said it will refuse outbound mail ballots from states that don't submit recipient information through its portal and meet the envelope and barcode requirements. Both figures are worth holding in mind: the volume is enormous, and proven fraud in the existing system has been rare. An appeal is expected quickly and the case could reach the Supreme Court again before ballots are mailed. If the White House wants durable reform rather than a headline, it should win these fights in the off-year, in statute, with lead time. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said there is "nothing magic" about the milestone and that the government "can grow our way out of that." Brett Loper of the Peter G. Peterson Foundation countered that doing so would take "gangbusters 4.3% growth every single year," which he called "all but unattainable." The economy grew 2.1% last year and 2.8% the year before. Treasury confirmed this month a $1.8 trillion deficit over the first 10 months of fiscal 2026. Former Speaker Paul Ryan: "You have to keep your nominal GDP growing ahead of your servicing costs, so that you can stabilize the debt ... but you can't grow your way out of total debt reduction," adding that Social Security and Medicare reform is unavoidable — "There's no getting around that." The Situation CBO, the Federal Reserve, and the Blue Chip forecaster survey all project annual growth at or below 2% for the next decade — meaning growth would have to roughly double for Bessent's math to work. The debt first crossed $1 trillion in 1981. The last balanced budgets ran from fiscal 1998 through fiscal 2001. Former Rep. Carolyn Bourdeaux (D-GA), now at the Concord Coalition: "There's zero chance we're going to be able to grow our way out of this right now, given the current deficits that we run." Caleb Quakenbush of the Bipartisan Policy Center noted the last comparable debt load came right after World War II, but that an aging population now pressures entitlements, with AI's effect on long-run growth "a huge question mark." The PerspectiveGrowth is necessary and it is not sufficient — and the people saying so loudest here are Republicans, not the left. Paul Ryan and the Peterson crowd are making the case fiscal conservatives have made for thirty years: you cannot outrun compound interest on $40 trillion at multiyear-high yields while spending keeps climbing. A $1.8 trillion deficit in ten months is not a growth problem, it's a spending problem, and pretending otherwise from the Treasury podium sets up the next administration to inherit a bill nobody can pay. Conservatives should hold their own side to the standard they'd apply to Democrats: name the cuts, reform the entitlement math, and stop treating a $40 trillion milestone as a rounding error. | | | There are only two things in life that are certain: death and taxes. But while we can’t escape death, we can at least try to reduce our tax burden. Even if you got a refund on your taxes this year, you probably had a big chunk of your income taken out from each paycheck. Wouldn’t it be nice if you could keep more of your own money, and put that money to good use? What many retirement savings don’t know is that gold (the popular safe haven asset) can be owned both inside and outside of IRA accounts, with differing tax treatments for each method. **Here are 3 ways that owning gold in a gold IRA could potentially save you a fortune on your taxes...**
---
**1\. Potential for Increased After-Tax Returns
** Depending on your income level and expected tax bracket in retirement, owning gold in a Traditional gold IRA can increase your after-tax returns on your gold holdings, compared to gold investments held in a brokerage account or a Roth IRA. **2\. Tax-Free Rollovers
** A gold IRA can be funded with a tax-free rollover from a 401(k), 403(b), TSP, IRA, or similar account, allowing you to use your existing tax-advantaged savings to buy gold without having to take a tax hit by distributing funds first. **3\. Tax-Deferred Growth
** Gold IRAs allow your gold to grow in value without having to pay taxes until you take a distribution in retirement. That could mean decades of tax-free wealth gains.
---
If you’re looking for ways to keep your hard-earned money safe from taxation, maybe it’s time to start looking at how a gold IRA could help you. The good news is, there’s a new guide that could help learn everything you need to know about Gold IRA’s. It’s the [**Beginner’s Guide to Gold IRAs****.**](https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.com/click/e116537/VaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cucHJvdGVjdGluZ215c2F2aW5ncy1lbWFpbC5jb20vYmVnaW5uZXJzLWd1aWRlLTA1MjQyNC8/SZW1haWxfZnJlZXRoaW5rZXJkYWlseV9jb20yNjA4Mjg/LbmNsYmdBdTNCNw/qP2NuPTg1NS01ODktNzQ3MyZscz0wMDEtRW1haWwtMXN0LVBhcnR5LUZyZWUtVGhpbmtlci1EYWlseSZzZmNpZD03MDFRaDAwMDAwc1VzbjU/gapHrQA/seo70549307)**** In this all-encompassing, informative guide, you’ll learn...

This experiment could cost New York taxpayers roughly $206 million in its first few years. Here is the problem in plain terms. Grocery stores operate on a razor-thin profit margin, somewhere between 1% and 3%. Mamdani is promising a 30% discount on a core basket of everyday groceries. That gap does not vanish. Taxpayers cover it. I left Cuba to escape exactly this kind of thinking.
The government decides what you buy, at what price, and the bill lands on the people who can least afford it. I have seen where it leads, and it does not lead to full shelves. clean_body: Friends, I ran the numbers on Zohran Mamdani's government-owned grocery store plan. The New York Post picked up the story, because the numbers are that bad. | Friends, I ran the numbers on Zohran Mamdani's government-owned grocery store plan. The New York Post picked up the story, because the numbers are that bad. | This experiment could cost New York taxpayers roughly $206 million in its first few years. Here is the problem in plain terms. Grocery stores operate on a razor-thin profit margin, somewhere between 1% and 3%. Mamdani is promising a 30% discount on a core basket of everyday groceries. That gap does not vanish. Taxpayers cover it. I left Cuba to escape exactly this kind of thinking. The government decides what you buy, at what price, and the bill lands on the people who can least afford it. I have seen where it leads, and it does not lead to full shelves. I will be that watchdog, but only if we win. | Through New York's matching program, a $10 donation becomes $70. _**By Eric J. Lullove, DPM -- Corresponding Medical Editor for Blue Amp Media**_
Just a couple of weeks ago, this publication laid out what the reporting then supported about the Hope Florida affair and drew a careful line around what remained unproven. The central question--whether $10 million clawed back from a Medicaid contractor had been lawfully redirected or improperly converted to political use--could not be answered from the outside. A grand jury had reportedly weighed it. Its findings sat sealed. We wrote that a complete evidentiary record was the only thing that would settle it, and that the officials with standing to open that record were the ones staying quiet.
That record is now public. And it does not equivocate.
A Florida statewide grand jury found that state officials misappropriated $10 million in taxpayer money--funds owed back to the program that insures Florida's poor children--and routed them, through a charity tied to First Lady Casey DeSantis, into political committees that spent the money to defeat a 2024 ballot measure. The panel called it "a sophisticated scheme to fund political activities." Then, having found the money was taken, it declined to charge anyone.1,2
The report was filed under seal on January 28 and stayed hidden for seven months. It became public this week only because _**CBS News Miami**_ investigative reporter Jim DeFede obtained a copy, and the Florida Center for Government Accountability--which had gone to court seeking merely to confirm the case existed--published it. For a health-care policy audience, the substance matters more than the drama of its release. So let's take the substance first.1
* * *
_**Cliff 's Note:**_
##### Eric Lullove is a practicing physician. He is not a political reporter, and nobody assigned him to spend his week reading a grand jury presentment that the state of Florida kept sealed for seven months. He did it because $10 million that belonged to poor kids' Medicaid ended up in a political committee, and because somebody ought to explain what that means to people who actually understand how health care gets paid for.
##### That's the whole model. No advertiser asked for this piece. No corporate parent had to bless it. No one had to worry about access. You paid for it, and that is the only reason it exists.

The 84-year-old senator hasn't appeared publicly since June 14. He hasn't been back to the Capitol, and hasn't taken a single vote. No one has said when he'll return.

Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold.
Families were being torn apart.
Lives were being destroyed. **I couldn't forget it.** **I couldn't stay silent.** I kept asking myself one question: **"What if it were my child?"** That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film _Sound of Freedom_. **Not for fame.**
**Not for awards.**
**But because I believed people needed to see the truth.** For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up. **But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.** And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**. Our mission is simple: **To stop the sale of God's children.**

| | | Team: You can make a big impact by sending a short letter today. Following the Supreme Court's ruling in _Louisiana v. Callais_ \-- **which gutted key Voting Rights Act protections and enabled extreme gerrymandering** \-- our democracy faces a critical threat. The decision actively strips political power from communities of color. In response, defenders of democracy and civil rights in the U.S. House of Representatives have introduced H.Res. 1384. Peter, **This week, we helped secure a settlement of up to $17 billion from Meta, the company that owns Facebook and Instagram.** I joined Attorneys General from across the country in suing Meta over allegations that the company knowingly failed to protect children on its platforms. The result is the largest Big Tech settlement in history. For Washington, the settlement will provide at least **$237 million to help enforce consumer protections and address the mental health impacts of social media on young people** , with the potential for nearly _**$339 million over the next decade.**_ It also means real changes to how Meta designs its products for kids and teens, including time limits, nighttime restrictions, stronger age verification, safer content controls, and limits on features tied to harmful social comparison. I’ve pushed for years to crack down on addictive social media features that keep kids scrolling at the expense of sleep, school, and their mental health, including trying to get stronger protections through the Legislature but couldn’t get them across the finish line. Now, Meta will be required to make changes that are in some ways even stronger. That matters. Companies as powerful as Meta should not be able to design products that harm kids and then avoid accountability. **As Attorney General, I’ll keep taking on powerful corporations when Washington families are paying the price.** Thank you for being part of this, Nick P.S. Teammates, 67 days. That is all we have left, and every single one of them counts. Team Cait is out across NY-17 every day, knocking doors and talking directly with voters about what is at stake this November. The energy we are seeing across this district is real, but we need more people on the ground to make this happen. This race will be decided by who shows up — and we need you out there with us. This is about more than flipping a seat. It is about sending someone to Congress who will actually fight to lower costs, take on corruption, and make sure Hudson Valley families have a real shot at the American Dream. Hope to see you out on the field! Team Cait

| | As of today, the war with Iran has lasted exactly 6 months. And what do we have to show for it?
* The deaths of 18 U.S. service members and thousands more civilians in the Middle East
* A massive global spike in oil prices, which is leading to more inflation across the board
* Showing that Iran has immense tactical leverage through the Strait of Hormuz

Needless death. Higher costs. And _zero_ strategic gains. **That's the legacy of Trump's war that Republicans in Congress have shamefully allowed to last for half a year.** The American people _did not want this war._ And the Trump administration didn't even attempt to explain the rationale. Instead, we all woke up 6 months ago to the sudden news that our country was in a war of _choice_. Perhaps Trump was desperate to distract from his already-unpopular economic agenda, or the outrage at his cover-up of the Epstein files. Perhaps Pete Hegseth was desperate to show "warrior ethos," and a bored Trump was convinced. **But one thing's for certain: their reckless decisions have put us on course to make the same mistakes as in Iraq.** I voted against that war, almost 24 years ago. Our country learned the hard way that military operations overseas in the name of nebulously defined "regime change" can go terribly awry and drag on indefinitely. There is still time to prevent this current war from spiraling further — but every day that Congress refuses to rein in Trump, it gets harder. **So we must keep demanding an end to Trump's illegal war. In 67 days, we have the chance to send Senate Republicans packing by electing progressive leaders who will stand up to Trump's agenda of chaos.** We must continue to call out the lies that lead to nothing but death. And we must ensure that this time, the tragic lessons of recent history aren't so quickly forgotten. | | **This month marked 91 years since the creation of Social Security.** On August 14, 1935, the monumental 37-page Social Security Act was signed by President Franklin D. Roosevelt. And now, most Americans do not remember a time before Social Security. In the years since its adoption, the landmark legislation has evolved into a euphemism for retirement benefits. But it is more than just a monthly check for retirees - **it is a safety net for**** _everyone_****that provides financial stability and peace of mind throughout life.** Social Security includes: **Retirement Security:** The most common connotation of Social Security is the safeguards for the retired. It ensures that your hard work is rewarded with a reliable income stream in our golden years. It is a promise of dignity and independence after a lifetime of work and contributions to your community's economy. **Disability Protection:** Life is unpredictable, and an unexpected disability can lead to financial strain. Social Security includes disability benefits that offer a lifeline to protect you and your family during challenging times. **Survivor Benefits:** Tragedy can strike, leaving loved ones in dire financial straits. Social Security provides crucial support to surviving spouses and dependents, easing the burden and helping them move forward. **Whether you are nearing retirement or just starting your career, understanding and supporting Social Security is vital.** But Social Security and its beneficiaries are vulnerable right now. The Big Ugly Law has made catastrophic cuts to important programs like Social Security. I am furious about the devastating cuts Republicans have rushed through this year with the Big Ugly Law. **To me, it is plain and simple: hardworking folks paid into Social Security, and it is not a handout.** I oppose the privatization of Social Security and support proposals that make the benefit formula more generous, use cost-of-living formulas that consider the expenses of seniors' purchases, and preserve Social Security for the future by scrapping the cap on income subject to Social Security taxes. **Social Security demonstrates our shared commitment to ensuring a dignified life for**** _everyone_****, regardless of their socioeconomic status.** And as a long-time advocate for strengthening Social Security, I am redoubling my efforts to fortify these protections. clean_body: We must educate and advocate for policies that enhance Social Security's longevity and effectiveness. | | | | This month marked 91 years since the creation of Social Security. On August 14, 1935, the monumental 37-page Social Security Act was signed by President Franklin D. Roosevelt. And now, most Americans do not remember a time before Social Security. In the years since its adoption, the landmark legislation has evolved into a euphemism for retirement benefits. But it is more than just a monthly check for retirees - it is a safety net for everyonethat provides financial stability and peace of mind throughout life. Social Security includes: Retirement Security: The most common connotation of Social Security is the safeguards for the retired. It ensures that your hard work is rewarded with a reliable income stream in our golden years. It is a promise of dignity and independence after a lifetime of work and contributions to your community's economy. Disability Protection: Life is unpredictable, and an unexpected disability can lead to financial strain. Social Security includes disability benefits that offer a lifeline to protect you and your family during challenging times. Survivor Benefits: Tragedy can strike, leaving loved ones in dire financial straits. Social Security provides crucial support to surviving spouses and dependents, easing the burden and helping them move forward. Whether you are nearing retirement or just starting your career, understanding and supporting Social Security is vital. But Social Security and its beneficiaries are vulnerable right now. The Big Ugly Law has made catastrophic cuts to important programs like Social Security. I am furious about the devastating cuts Republicans have rushed through this year with the Big Ugly Law. To me, it is plain and simple: hardworking folks paid into Social Security, and it is not a handout. I oppose the privatization of Social Security and support proposals that make the benefit formula more generous, use cost-of-living formulas that consider the expenses of seniors' purchases, and preserve Social Security for the future by scrapping the cap on income subject to Social Security taxes. Social Security demonstrates our shared commitment to ensuring a dignified life for everyone, regardless of their socioeconomic status. And as a long-time advocate for strengthening Social Security, I am redoubling my efforts to fortify these protections. = = It is not just about us. It is about future generations, too. Together, we can ensure that Social Security remains a rock-solid foundation for all Americans. | | Friend,

I got my start in organizing at age 16, and by 19 I was the Executive Director of the Young Women’s Freedom Center.

I worked day in and day out with young people who had been handed the short end of the stick by society. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138119734/643043612/1833629142?refcode=cls-em-fr-20260828-EOM1-365do-img&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDQ0NDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzA1ZWFkNzQtMjlhMy1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=gAGhn_EvA3e6L_bzAwr51UqyPO9wqlFz1aGfYeTjKtI=) Whether it was poverty, the legal system, foster care, or living on the street, I watched brilliant, promising young women overcome the challenges of a system designed to discard them.

What I learned then, and what I know now, is that the best leaders come from the bottom up, not the top down.

30 years later, I am still fighting to build a world where our young people get to grow old.

I’ve sponsored bills to raise the minimum wage, provide universal childcare, and expand Social Security.

I’ve secured more than $870 million in federal funding for the East Bay.

And I’m still using my voice to call out the ways that our economy is rigged against working people.

**I didn’t run for Congress because I enjoy asking people for money._[But the truth is, every dollar we raise helps build a progressive majority and deliver real results in 2027. Hey folks,
The Tate brothers' latest bond hearing was an absolute disaster--and their excuses are getting more desperate by the day.
Their lawyer is throwing everything at the wall, the manosphere is trying to manufacture outrage, and the political protection they thought they had isn't looking nearly as strong anymore. This one tells us a lot about accountability, influence, and what happens when the online persona finally collides with the legal system.
* [**00:01:24**] The bond hearing fallout--and why the Tate brothers' lawyer is scrambling for a new argument.
* [**00:04:00**] The plea for sympathy involving Tristan Tate's family gets a blunt response: responsibility has to start somewhere.
* [**00:06:35**] Their lawyer argues the Romanian proceedings create "special circumstances," but the argument starts falling apart fast.
* [**00:09:00**] The manosphere tries to turn the Tates into gladiators--and the actual protest outside the detention facility tells a very different story.
* [**00:11:41**] What happens next: the bond decision, Marco Rubio's extradition call, the UK case, and why this story is bigger than two internet personalities.

This isn't just about Andrew and Tristan Tate. It's about money, manufactured influence, political connections, and whether people can build an online empire big enough to escape accountability. I'm staying on this story because it exposes something much bigger about power and the legal and political systems in Trump's America. **If you value independent coverage that keeps following the story after everyone else moves on, help me keep it going.**

In that time we’ve teamed up with NYC public housing developments, community organizations, and more to give thousands of kids a strong start to the school year with pencils, pens, crayons, erasers, notebooks, rulers, and a backpack. We’re hoping to purchase one more round of backpacks and supplies before this year’s drive ends. We’ve run the numbers and it costs our team $8-$10 to put together one backpack filled with school supplies. Your donation today will mean a child without school supplies can start the year with their head held high. Thank you! If you have an extra minute or two, I’d love to share this story with you.
When I moved to Oregon in 1987, right off an Amtrak train from the East Coast to rainy Eugene, I was excited about a new place to explore and find new friends. As I settled in, I found much more — a place where I could truly be myself. I fell in love with the beauty of the state and the openness of the people. I had found a community I could call home.
My journey eventually led me to nonprofit advocacy work at Oregon Food Bank and then Children First for Oregon — fighting hunger, supporting financial stability for more people, and strengthening state policies around childcare for working families and healthcare for kids.
Through that work — listening to Oregonians, working on issues our communities were facing, and helping create real solutions — I realized I could make an even bigger difference through elected public service. [That led me to nearly 15 years of service in the Oregon legislature.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138120132/643044770/1974481312?amounts=5,10,15,25,50,100,250&amount=5&refcode=email_082826_beforetheweekendbio&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjYWRkNDI0My0yYmEzLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ih6aPi2wisD9EepEVdGrT4kuW1HhDeGGUYdySBEKawM=)
As Governor, my focus remains the same: listening to Oregonians, tackling our biggest challenges, and building a stronger, brighter future for all of us.
But the work is far from over, especially now with all the challenges that President Trump and a Republican-led Congress have put in our path.
In the past year alone, President Trump has tried to send Oregon National Guard troops into Portland, sent ICE to terrorize our communities, cut SNAP food assistance for our vulnerable neighbors, attacked our vote-by-mail system, and threatened reproductive freedoms.
[_My opponent, Christine Drazan, has stood with President Trump every step of the way._](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138120133/643044771/1974481312?amounts=5,10,15,25,50,100,250&amount=5&refcode=email_082826_beforetheweekendbio&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjYWRkNDI0My0yYmEzLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ih6aPi2wisD9EepEVdGrT4kuW1HhDeGGUYdySBEKawM=)
I believe Oregon deserves a governor who will always stand up for our state. And if you believe that too, then I need your support today.

clean_body: Governors are the last line of defense for so much that we care about = Peter, = That’s why I want to remind you why I ran for Governor in the first place. = | | = If you have an extra minute or two, I’d love to share this story with you. When I moved to Oregon in 1987, right off an Amtrak train from the East Coast to rainy Eugene, I was excited about a new place to explore and find new friends. As I settled in, I found much more — a place where I could truly be myself. I fell in love with the beauty of the state and the openness of the people. I had found a community I could call home. My journey eventually led me to nonprofit advocacy work at Oregon Food Bank and then Children First for Oregon — fighting hunger, supporting financial stability for more people, and strengthening state policies around childcare for working families and healthcare for kids. Through that work — listening to Oregonians, working on issues our communities were facing, and helping create real solutions — I realized I could make an even bigger difference through elected public service. = As Governor, my focus remains the same: listening to Oregonians, tackling our biggest challenges, and building a stronger, brighter future for all of us. But the work is far from over, especially now with all the challenges that President Trump and a Republican-led Congress have put in our path. In the past year alone, President Trump has tried to send Oregon National Guard troops into Portland, sent ICE to terrorize our communities, cut SNAP food assistance for our vulnerable neighbors, attacked our vote-by-mail system, and threatened reproductive freedoms. = I believe Oregon deserves a governor who will always stand up for our state. | | Dear Peter,

As we get ready to head into the weekend and wrap up the month of August, I just wanted to give you a quick update on where things stand in my race for re-election as Nevada Controller.

The good news is that my campaign continues to build strength. Voters I’m talking to appreciate my successful efforts to promote transparency in state government, and they’re excited about my pledge to continue to do the same in a second term.

The bad news is that the overall political environment remains a challenging one at this point for Republicans. The numbers vary among different polls, but the picture shows clearly that Democrats right now have a consistent lead in the generic ballot test.

This should serve as an important reminder: Even with my strong record, winning re-election this year won’t be easy. Nevada remains a very competitive state, and if we’re going to prevail this fall, we’re going to need to overcome the political climate to a significant degree.

If you’re able to support me today with a [contribution](https://us.list-manage.com/pyYNujXGcdF?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73) to my campaign, it will help ensure we have the resources to do exactly that.

[You can contribute by clicking here.](https://us.list-manage.com/bOXh22uzVTh?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73)

Make no mistake: I’m very confident about my chances this November. But I also know that we cannot take anything for granted. Everything we’ve accomplished these past few years for the cause of transparent, accountable government is in danger if Democrats capture the Controller’s Office.

We can’t let that happen.

My friend, you’ve been so generous in your support for me and my campaign, and I cannot tell you how grateful I am.

If you can, I hope you’ll consider [another contribution today](https://us.list-manage.com/PvMQVArOUht?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73), and help me continue to build the critical momentum we’ll need heading into the stretch run of this campaign.

Thank you so much for your support, and for your commitment to our shared principles.

For Nevada’s future,

Andy

Hello -

My name is Mary Peltola, and after winning our open primary, I am officially running in the general election for United States Senate in Alaska.

I want to share with you why I made the decision to run – and to ask for your support as we begin the general election together.

But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you’re ready to join our fight for fish, family, and freedom, please use this button to split a contribution between my campaign for U.S. Senate and Patty Murray:

Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision.

When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.

Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.

Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.

So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families.

And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don’t even believe us. They're focused on their own wallets – not ours.

And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.

It’s why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.

I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.

My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning.

But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.

I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future.

**This is going to be the closest and most consequential Senate race this year, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we’ll be able to flip this seat... and that is together.**

So I am asking:

subject: A Brooklyn girl with a library card

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260828-2-partner_ms_tish_em_demandjustice.i1uFnB&refcode=em20260828-61763&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1001&akid=61763%2E1407376%2E5q8YF6 ]A picture of Letitia James as a child.

When I was a young girl in Brooklyn, I spent hours in the public library.

I didn’t know it at the time, but those quiet afternoons would shape the
rest of my life. Because it was there that I discovered Thurgood Marshall.

I read about a man who used the law to break down segregation. A man who
understood that justice isn’t abstract — it’s something you fight for,
every day, for real people.

And that is what this moment is asking of us now.

Across this country, we are seeing efforts to undermine the rule of law,
to concentrate power, and to intimidate those who dare to stand up and
speak out.

But I want you to hear me clearly: I will not capitulate. I will not bow.
I will not break. And I will not bend.

If you’re with me, I’m asking you to be part of this work. Because it
takes resources to take on powerful interests and win — and I cannot do
this alone.

subject: Democracy doesn’t protect itself
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Voto Latino
body:
10 weeks left to make an impact.
#
Democracy doesn’t just protect itself, Peter.
It depends on people who are willing to fight for it — and right now, that fight is more important than ever.
With the Supreme Court’s recent decision allowing new restrictions on mail-in voting to move forward, **millions of voters could face even greater barriers to participating in our democracy this fall.** At a moment when access to the ballot is under direct threat, we can’t afford to sit on the sidelines.
**That’s why Voto Latino is staying focused on protecting voter participation, expanding access to the ballot box, and making sure our communities have the tools they need to make their voices heard. But we can’t do it alone.**
We need grassroots supporters like you to help fund our work – especially as we head into the last 10 weeks of this election cycle.
**That’s why we set a goal of raising $25,000 by August 31st to help power this critical work.**
**[If you believe every eligible voter deserves a fair chance to participate, will you chip in $3 to help us reach our end-of-month fundraising goal so we can keep fighting for our democracy?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260828-2.GWnDCc&amount=3&refcode=em20260828-525&t=1&akid=525%2E1366028%2EVP0WJ1)**

It doesn’t put anything into effect to impact the midterm election. **What is the executive order trying to do?** Right now, the Trump administration is fighting to implement an [executive order](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138121590/643048517/1154225960?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVjAwMS8xLzgyNzA0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjkyNTBiYTVmLTJkYTMtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMjI0ODJhOWE4ZCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=gFYgPsW--B3YvZTY8ACU-qIQSDksRfUtsDucuYFVMUc=&emci=13c37681-e8a2-f111-9b33-0022482a9a8d&emdi=9250ba5f-2da3-f111-9b33-0022482a9a8d&ceid=4069003) that would create lists of eligible voters and instruct the USPS to only deliver ballots to voters on that list. Peter, we had a historic grassroots volunteer effort in the
primary election. Even now, Team Abdul continues to grow. Thousands of
people have been chattering and getting organized in our volunteer Slack
community. Now we’re ready to get everybody — every single person —
talking to voters again at their doors and over the phone.

This weekend, Abdul’s Regional Organizers are partnering up with One Team
Michigan to host some exciting neighborhood canvasses. Whether you’re
picking back up from the primary, canvassing for the first time, or you’ve
been knocking doors all along, come meet our organizers and other
passionate volunteers who will be the key to beating back MAGA in Michigan
and get some priceless conversations in with Michigan voters.

FUN FACT: 100% of dogs support Abdul

We need to hit the ground running because we’re less than 10 weeks away
from Election Day. Mike Rogers and his corporate allies have been flooding
the airwaves with misinformation for months already. Direct voter contact
is how we’ll set the record straight.

Stay up to date on all Team Abdul events at
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1613?t=1012&akid=3055%2E251025%2Ehs-sKg ]https://a4-m.org/TeamAbdul

TEAM ABDUL EVENTS

If you can’t make it in person, we’re [ http://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1579?t=1013&akid=3055%2E251025%2Ehs-sKg ]phonebanking almost every day.
Join from anywhere.

[ http://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1579?t=1014&akid=3055%2E251025%2Ehs-sKg ]PHONEBANK

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

It’s going to take a coordinated, nationwide effort of Democrats to push
back against record breaking corporate spending in Michigan. It doesn’t
matter how much time you can give, if you put all of yourself into that
time.

Click a link, take a shift and help us get closer to a future where Money
out of Politics, Money in your Pockets, and Medicare for All is not just a
slogan, but the reality for every American.

We look forward to meeting you,
Abdul’s Organizing Team

P.S. Slack is where our volunteers self-organize. It’s the place to get in
contact with Abdul’s staff, volunteer leadership, and other supporters.

On Monday, U.S. Senators Katie (Boyd) Britt (R-Ala.) and Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.) introduced a bipartisan bill to expand early detection of colorectal cancer.

The Colorectal Cancer Early Detection Act would help address a rise in colorectal cancer rates in younger Americans. According to recent studies cited by Britt and Osoff, colorectal cancer is now the leading cause of cancer-related death for Americans under 50 years old, despite being highly preventable and treatable when detected early. “The staggering rise in colorectal cancer we're seeing across the country demands action. We know that this especially aggressive cancer is affecting younger Americans now more than ever. We must give states and healthcare providers the resources they need to better inform and treat the public, which is why I'm proud to introduce this legislation with Senator Ossoff,” said Britt.

name: Pete Maysmith, LCV
subject: Peter, here’s why I’m hopeful
body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM5MjExMzAS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjUyMDE0MjA2OAS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
Peter, The midterms are fast approaching, and honestly, I’m feeling hopeful. Not because the road ahead will be easy — it won’t. But because LCV and our 30
state affiliates — the Conservation Voters Movement — have something powerful on
our side: real solutions to the most pressing problems everyday Americans are
facing. Recently, I spoke with journalist Terry Moran about LCV’s work creating and
driving these solutions. We talked about some of the challenges we’re all facing
right now: sky high utility bills, extreme weather fueled by climate change,
surging data centers depleting our resources and jacking up costs, and the clean
energy transition we all need. You can watch that interview here. https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/4L4XBdzAwpfZ/WDFZOXljUW10Zkd4dHV5UTU2M0xRWEJNaUI0dTJFRVZOcWJnQVlHSFVOQThueFJnY1V6bVpkTUw0eGZlVzlxYi9uM2RHMlozNm9ndzlOeCtqYy83d1RtZnpremh2TTd1TW1Oc1ZSN2p4SXc9S0/ Families shouldn’t have to choose between paying their utility bills and putting
food on the table. Communities shouldn’t have to breathe polluted air or worry
about the next climate disaster. But these are the realities Americans are facing. And we know who to blame:
Trump and his congressional Republican enablers. The cost of utility bills alone
is up 18% since Trump came into office! And remember, he promised to cut them in
half. These are the issues that matter most to people’s everyday lives — and guess
what? They’re also environmental issues. I’m optimistic because I know that when people learn that LCV has solutions to
make life safer, healthier, and more affordable for everyone, we win. Clean energy is just one example. For a long time, clean energy was considered a
luxury, but that’s no longer the case. Today, wind, solar, and battery storage
are the cheapest and fastest ways to power our future — and they’re better for
our health, our climate, and our wallets. Across the country, LCV and our state affiliates are delivering this message.
We’re working hard to reach energy bill voters — and data shows that 51% of
swing voters in the most competitive races are motivated by their utility bills. If we can reach these voters before November, we will see climate champions
elected into Congress and up and down ballots across the country. These are the
people we can count on to advance the policies that protect us all. And that’s why I’m so hopeful, Peter. The Trump administration wants us to feel powerless. But our optimism and
commitment to protecting people and our planet are exactly where our power comes
from. I know that together, we have the power to win. I am so proud to do this work alongside my colleagues at LCV and our state
partners, and alongside you. Thank you for being with us. With fierce commitment, Pete Maysmith

President

body:
Another thing absolutely NO ONE asked for. | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138122687/643052085/-785282667?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlMGEzMmYxOC0zMmEzLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=uSL7ri5fpaEL_4TczyiebYzOi9aWBHwSRdnZFwihFAA=)

Peter, It's Becca. Okay. I have to talk about this because I genuinely cannot believe this is where we are. **Yesterday, Donald Trump signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario “Lake America.”** _Yes. Really._ I promise you, in all my conversations with Vermonters about what they need from their government, **not one person has ever pulled me aside and said, “Becca, please do something about the name of Lake Ontario.”** You know what people DO talk to me about? Groceries. Gas. Rent. Healthcare. Childcare. Whether there’s enough money left in the checking account after the bills clear. **Donald Trump ran for president promising to bring costs down. Instead, Americans are watching their grocery bills climb while he spends his time on a giant White House ballroom, obsessing over the Reflecting Pool, and now apparently rebranding the Great Lakes.** Come on now. This is just getting ridiculous. [_**If you’re as fed up as I am watching this administration waste time on vanity projects while families are struggling to afford the basics, chip in $10, $25, or whatever makes sense today. Help me keep fighting for a government that actually has its priorities straight.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138122688/643052086/687249955?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlMGEzMmYxOC0zMmEzLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=uSL7ri5fpaEL_4TczyiebYzOi9aWBHwSRdnZFwihFAA=) **[ENOUGH WITH THE VANITY PROJECTS!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138122689/643052087/687249955?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlMGEzMmYxOC0zMmEzLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=uSL7ri5fpaEL_4TczyiebYzOi9aWBHwSRdnZFwihFAA=)** Here’s the part that really gets me. There are families standing in grocery store aisles right now doing mental math. Maybe we skip the meat this week. Maybe we put that back. Maybe we can stretch this until payday. There are people seeing the total at the gas pump and wincing. People postponing a doctor’s appointment because they cannot afford another bill. Parents trying to figure out how to make childcare work without blowing up the family budget. **Lake Ontario was doing just fine. It did not need a rebrand or an executive order. And frankly, the American people deserve a government with priorities more serious than whatever happens to be flattering Donald Trump’s ego that afternoon.** **I’m in Congress because I believe government should actually make people’s lives better. Lower healthcare costs. More affordable housing. Strong public schools. Good-paying jobs. An economy where buying groceries does not require a strategy session.** That work may not come with a giant gold sign. _And I’m okay with that. But it does take people willing to fight for it. _ [_**So if you’re tired of watching Donald Trump waste everyone’s time on monuments to himself while families are getting squeezed, I’m asking you to stand with me. Pitch in $5, $10, $25, or whatever you can today and help me keep fighting for a government that puts working people ahead of one man’s ego.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138122690/643052088/687249955?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlMGEzMmYxOC0zMmEzLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=uSL7ri5fpaEL_4TczyiebYzOi9aWBHwSRdnZFwihFAA=) And for the record: I’ll still be calling it Lake Ontario with the rest of you. — Becca

clean_body: Another thing absolutely NO ONE asked for. | = Peter, It's Becca. Okay. I have to talk about this because I genuinely cannot believe this is where we are. Yesterday, Donald Trump signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario “Lake America.” Yes. Really. I promise you, in all my conversations with Vermonters about what they need from their government, not one person has ever pulled me aside and said, “Becca, please do something about the name of Lake Ontario.” You know what people DO talk to me about? Groceries. Gas. Rent. Healthcare. Childcare. Whether there’s enough money left in the checking account after the bills clear. Donald Trump ran for president promising to bring costs down. Instead, Americans are watching their grocery bills climb while he spends his time on a giant White House ballroom, obsessing over the Reflecting Pool, and now apparently rebranding the Great Lakes. Come on now. This is just getting ridiculous. = = Here’s the part that really gets me. There are families standing in grocery store aisles right now doing mental math. Maybe we skip the meat this week. Maybe we put that back. Maybe we can stretch this until payday. There are people seeing the total at the gas pump and wincing. People postponing a doctor’s appointment because they cannot afford another bill. Parents trying to figure out how to make childcare work without blowing up the family budget. Lake Ontario was doing just fine. It did not need a rebrand or an executive order. And frankly, the American people deserve a government with priorities more serious than whatever happens to be flattering Donald Trump’s ego that afternoon. I’m in Congress because I believe government should actually make people’s lives better. Lower healthcare costs. More affordable housing. Strong public schools. Good-paying jobs. An economy where buying groceries does not require a strategy session. That work may not come with a giant gold sign. And I’m okay with that. But it does take people willing to fight for it. = And for the record: I’ll still be calling it Lake Ontario with the rest of you. — Becca If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = mailto:beccabalintvt@beccabalint.com | Paid for by Becca Balint for Vermont P.O. _**Peter**_ , I want to tell you about the town I grew up in. Jackson, Georgia isn’t the kind of place that makes national news very often. It’s not a big city. It doesn’t have a famous skyline or a professional sports team. What it has is something a whole lot more valuable, and a whole lot harder to replace. _**It's the kind of town where July 4th is still a big deal.**_ Where folks put flags on their porches not because somebody told them to, **but because they genuinely mean it. ** Where the hardware store owner knows your daddy's name, and where people still hold the door open for strangers without thinking twice about it. Where you can still hear a crowd go quiet when Taps plays at the cemetery. Where the old veterans in the parade get the loudest applause every single time, because every single person standing on that sidewalk understands what those men and women gave up so the rest of us could be there. _That's the America I grew up in._ And I'll tell you, I never took a single day of it for granted. _**Peter**_ , I think about that America every single day of this campaign. Because here's what I know about Jon Ossoff that I don't think gets said enough: **He doesn't represent that America. ** If he had his way, towns like Jackson would be quietly forgotten, **left behind in favor of the coastal elite's vision of what this country is supposed to look like. ** Diversity committees, government programs, and Washington bureaucrats deciding what's best for people they've never met and communities they've never set foot in. That's not a small disagreement about tax policy, **Peter**. That is a fundamental difference in what we believe America is supposed to be. This race is about policy, yes. **Ossoff's vote to skyrocket your grocery bill. ** **His vote to send stimulus checks to prisoners and illegal aliens. ** **His votes to let men compete in women's sports. ** **_Those things matter enormously, and I am going to fight him on every single one of them._** But underneath all of that, this race is about something bigger. **It's about what kind of America our kids and grandkids grow up in.** It's about whether the town where a little boy can watch veterans march down Main Street and feel something real in his chest can still exist in twenty years. I believe we can save that America. I believe it's worth every fight, every mile on the road, every dollar raised, and every prayer said between now and November. But I need you with me in this fight, Peter. **[Will you chip in today and help us fight for the America we both know is worth saving?](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=b33930e3e02e445d8e2953895558ba0d&_e=M9t0AKq_aRGaZps3tmZeULWufM8HK3d4LWPxGVbASZyAXr_lB8HQsIZjv_LMOJZzsVgMODZB3Nw3DswJ4sasQEOGHLlKDK-DY_Jh3uqWPM9jki5Q0Sr4nEYDbV3FoDH2IWBMdD-UzLwRMaCv3VaGuCg4EVI_9CIE3r5H79_z8IyBkdGghPN4AN4R-Q9Nb2BrJ1e1u0nhC0ZLupFl_OZRV1mU0CIgm8ozwAgl5YSQi85ekyfTOYfK4cMyGr_1WnJKh0xeYS0EU93UQyI-p5mp2lqu8ck9Q7-JKNdHk1gzp3E9fr_L-mwmaoJH67AyLjnnG81oNMmRDB4cO6yzx_iULnI3UpWhqtMskF5b1WVusKatTbhymOHvYf61yc525lj19CgBIbyFU7zu2IsTRoaB4psuF_Cqwxr-Un_CQq_SlyMbJLuunvQpRScE3e_F06Z2yyftILR9oTa8iDcJZzFN7EIHhq-RtZbI02YvvN8hTGnFkAW6zWbCk4wuInKjC1l5cMBM3pXH-oEZq3cSMEdf22B_aWzRH3Cge65Zk15k8eTpaC66bOCo7WX1tS4tsU_DYM8xG4y0PU04NUM0-ew2idf9XDdBGZRCIAwZCySEsDbMD4ilFdShd1c44JVNIPMLWGuhcyweIr3PzNpl597y0e7sSeJqEM32BPBPhDKs3BWpDiFsUaXOjpCJPwWVLckCv0viiCPAPOc098rWRl5yuiZwMS6tkF-d-QePtjDUnHE%3D)**

clean_body: Flags on porches. Taps at the cemetery. Veterans in the parade.| | | Peter , I want to tell you about the town I grew up in. Jackson, Georgia isn’t the kind of place that makes national news very often. It’s not a big city. It doesn’t have a famous skyline or a professional sports team. What it has is something a whole lot more valuable, and a whole lot harder to replace. It's the kind of town where July 4th is still a big deal. Where folks put flags on their porches not because somebody told them to, but because they genuinely mean it. Where the hardware store owner knows your daddy's name, and where people still hold the door open for strangers without thinking twice about it. Where you can still hear a crowd go quiet when Taps plays at the cemetery. Where the old veterans in the parade get the loudest applause every single time, because every single person standing on that sidewalk understands what those men and women gave up so the rest of us could be there. That's the America I grew up in. And I'll tell you, I never took a single day of it for granted. Peter , I think about that America every single day of this campaign. Because here's what I know about Jon Ossoff that I don't think gets said enough: He doesn't represent that America. If he had his way, towns like Jackson would be quietly forgotten, left behind in favor of the coastal elite's vision of what this country is supposed to look like. Diversity committees, government programs, and Washington bureaucrats deciding what's best for people they've never met and communities they've never set foot in. That's not a small disagreement about tax policy, Peter. That is a fundamental difference in what we believe America is supposed to be. This race is about policy, yes. Ossoff's vote to skyrocket your grocery bill. His vote to send stimulus checks to prisoners and illegal aliens. His votes to let men compete in women's sports. Those things matter enormously, and I am going to fight him on every single one of them. But underneath all of that, this race is about something bigger. It's about what kind of America our kids and grandkids grow up in. It's about whether the town where a little boy can watch veterans march down Main Street and feel something real in his chest can still exist in twenty years. I believe we can save that America. I believe it's worth every fight, every mile on the road, every dollar raised, and every prayer said between now and November. But I need you with me in this fight, Peter. Thanks, Peter , your support means everything to me. | | _With just eleven days until the primary, I am using each day to discuss an issue I have highlighted on the campaign trail. For Day 11, I am highlighting the need to build a just, humane, and functional immigration system._
* * *
Dear David, Business owners across NH-1 can’t find workers to keep their doors open. Families are being snatched from their homes on the way to work. ICE agents are killing people in the streets. **The system is broken, and cruelty is not a plan.** I have said “Abolish ICE” many times on the campaign trail, but for those words to be more than a slogan, we have to tell voters what comes next. **[In Congress, I’ll move to abolish ICE, fight for a real immigration system, a fair path to citizenship for people who have built their lives here, a functioning asylum and refugee process, and border security rooted in competence and humanity, not chaos and fear. Can you support this work by pitching in today?](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/Iq3xkc4jDrHA1kHG1HByFQ~~/AAUS1hA~/re0oibGbt5oZkTXdLpfP0DKVwUK9PH-FN1i8J5Atn0WWeQkawVIPUrs3-2YWaPZ-tSuPT56Ofth2OpK4KWUam5epIZKUioWPTQdzkjyZDWRx584mQl76OZc-vL4AlFVrWA441a55ejW3niAPmXoLwBeX4TIAhDGoKsapvEqjORhgV_eXJVcli_HPTLPCVgbpytA4QoPBdnX6H8IjduCO4qHKMDbyMM7f55Kq1YKIE7oDtvUq79rSFkETOmKPctOmFAESGEp2-bqLgCz_TDydQg~~)** | | [DONATE](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/Iq3xkc4jDrHA1kHG1HByFQ~~/AAUS1hA~/re0oibGbt5oZkTXdLpfP0DKVwUK9PH-FN1i8J5Atn0WWeQkawVIPUrs3-2YWaPZ-tSuPT56Ofth2OpK4KWUam5epIZKUioWPTQdzkjyZDWRx584mQl76OZc-vL4AlFVrWA441a55ejW3niAPmXoLwBeX4TIAhDGoKsapvEqjORhgV_eXJVcli_HPTLPCVgbpytA4QoPBdnX6H8IjduCO4qHKMDbyMM7f55Kq1YKIE7oDtvUq79rSFkETOmKPctOmFAESGEp2-bqLgCz_TDydQg~~)

**ICE is not a broken agency that needs fixing; it is an agency whose design produces the exact outcomes that we are now witnessing.**
When an institution is built to enforce a broken system without due process protections, without meaningful accountability, and with a culture that has consistently shielded agents from consequences for misconduct and killing, reform is insufficient. **The institution must be replaced.**
Abolishing ICE does not mean abolishing immigration enforcement. It means replacing a failed institution with one that is built from the ground up with civil rights protections, democratic accountability, and a mission that’s oriented toward a functional immigration system rather than fear and punishment.
Here’s what that looks like:
* **Replacing ICE** with a Civil Immigration Enforcement Agency (CIEA), reconstituted criminal immigration enforcement, independent immigration courts system, and Civil Detention Standards and Oversight Board.
* **Fixing the “No Line” problem** by creating legal pathways for residency, including expanding visa categories, modernizing the family reunification system, restoring and expanding asylum protections, and creating a path to permanent legal status for the approximately 11 million undocumented people currently living in the United States.
* **Reinvesting in border infrastructure** that actually works, including expanding processing capacity, immigration courts, asylum officers, and case management systems that can handle the volume of people seeking to enter the country through legal channels.
* **Restoring relationships with municipalities and states** by codifying the right of state and local governments to decline immigration enforcement partnerships, restoring federal funding that was withheld as coercion, and establishing a new framework for voluntary cooperation based on genuine community safety needs, not political pressure.
* **Reckoning with the harm that has already been done** by launching independent investigations into every death in ICE custody, compensating families separated by the Trump administration, repaying municipalities, counties, medical providers, and states that are owed money by ICE under existing contracts, and restoring legal status for people deported without due process and a mechanism for return for those who were wrongly removed.

I am running for Congress because local action, as necessary as it is, can only go so far. The comprehensive reform this country needs to abolish ICE and build a just system in its place, to create legal pathways to citizenship that reflect both our values and our reality, requires legislative power.

body:
ICYMI: SCOTUS just gave Trump another opening to continue his attacks on mail-in voting.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260828-3&t=1&akid=3941%2E587540%2EUReo06)
Peter,
**ICYMI: SCOTUS just gave Trump another opening to continue his attacks on mail-in voting.**
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260828_3_rr.JsL36e&refcode=em20260828-3941&t=2&akid=3941%2E587540%2EUReo06)
I’ll be honest — this is frustrating. In the middle of a critical midterm election cycle, Trump is pulling out all the stops to try and make it harder for every American to vote.
To be clear, this is not a final stamp of approval on Trump’s mail-in voting ban. It is, however, **an opening to further muddy the waters on a voting method that a third of the country relies on.**
And that’s what I’m angry about. Trump knows Republicans can't win the fair way, so he’s resorting to creating chaos and confusion right before an election, hoping people will be too confused or discouraged to turn out. It’s the same, tired playbook he’s used many times before.
**I’m going to let you in on something though, Peter: Trump and his allies are moving like this**** _because they’re terrified._******
They see the energy young people are bringing to the midterm cycle — the genuine hope for the future our slate of candidates has inspired in them.
They see the red seats we’re coming to flip, and they realize their grip on power is coming loose.
And listen, the reality is, the right has been working to suppress our voting rights _all year_. They came after LWD-endorsed candidate Justin J. Pearson, Trump-appointed justices led the gutting of the VRA, and now they’re targeting mail-in voting.

body:
A kid from 53206 who built a career on bringing people together | | | | [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquchf2e3e-bIm5hAkq2zKIjvamPfag9y_bswSQjaYCFy9MjdWE1wV2uXo3NcOqsJcFtgsV_KgISdRGF7nV1t9x3vQLdWPqNxbxiFkoFjYyB1J85MG6Z-Y_Wvw3iCqcVZ4mNYPtGCGEZ9CFA2TKBLiFkgKezujpLgui1j-0fcunkVio0HFm3AUGZfHysOMvoTfaBoHj5EhSpll4-4JSO7vs-uaqYTR8U_MAV0VoDD4g6htl7e2en6WzzLSchQ8IfQJLMCma42o0z4c7qMMQvbhLlO6fQ9DsH7bV98YgI1YfPPZP-lFvbjP-IkKRPLLuM5aILARXSd0FAu3swvZwYI_St6EbzOQlPeZPxwpoRwP_VEOt7B51GibT-kQGgVVQd5R1Mtaeo3IfFo8tE24UBB3gbBuE7bLFPwmq_CkLMFe5hjXzsDRbK5HnzjoGgtQP4zms/4tk/UPSUlvywTfmWXqxkT-HP_w/h0/h001.aCsDVBpCBSU-fOBkC4Xgq3pCMzFWCqgd0i3JJCg17FU) Derek, now that I'm Wisconsin's Democratic nominee for Governor, I wanted to take a minute to introduce myself properly. I grew up in Milwaukee's 53206 ZIP code, where my family faced food insecurity and the threat of eviction. **I know what it feels like when the system isn't built for people like me.** That's what got me into public service in the first place. I got my start in the Wisconsin Legislature, finding common ground with people I didn't always agree with to pass laws that actually helped people. Then I became Milwaukee County Executive, the youngest person and the first Black person to hold that office, where I brought together labor, business, and community organizations to build close to 1,000 units of affordable housing and push for universal childcare for working families. **I'm ready to take this same work ethic to the governor's office to make lives better for all Wisconsinites.** Wisconsin is one of the closest states in the country. clean_body: A kid from 53206 who built a career on bringing people together | | | | Derek, now that I'm Wisconsin's Democratic nominee for Governor, I wanted to take a minute to introduce myself properly. I grew up in Milwaukee's 53206 ZIP code, where my family faced food insecurity and the threat of eviction. I know what it feels like when the system isn't built for people like me. That's what got me into public service in the first place. I got my start in the Wisconsin Legislature, finding common ground with people I didn't always agree with to pass laws that actually helped people. Then I became Milwaukee County Executive, the youngest person and the first Black person to hold that office, where I brought together labor, business, and community organizations to build close to 1,000 units of affordable housing and push for universal childcare for working families. I'm ready to take this same work ethic to the governor's office to make lives better for all Wisconsinites. Wisconsin is one of the closest states in the country. Every one of our last three presidential elections was decided by less than a point. And my opponent? He's a far-right election denier who spent his time in Congress supporting Donald Trump and MAGA extremism.
